{"asset_classes":["crypto_perp"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"binance_perp_1d","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","close","quote_volume"],"frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"coinmetrics_supply_1d","description":"NEW DATASET (free, public, no API key): Coin Metrics Community API, endpoint https://community-api.coinmetrics.io/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics with metrics=SplyCur and frequency=1d. SplyCur is the current supply of the asset in native units, computed by Coin Metrics from the chain: the sum of all native units ever created and visible on the ledger, or the contract total supply for tokens. Wanted: one daily series per Binance USD-M perp base asset that Coin Metrics covers (BTC, ETH, LTC, BCH, XRP, ADA, DOT, SOL, LINK, UNI, AAVE, ... whatever the community tier serves), keyed by the Binance perp id (e.g. SOLUSDT.P) with the Binance-to-Coin-Metrics ticker map stored in the report. Ambiguous or reused tickers (a ticker that mapped to two different assets over time) should be dropped, not guessed. Clock crypto: Coin Metrics daily values are end of UTC day. The strategy reads them with a one-day lag anyway. History from the earliest available date (2019 or earlier wanted, so that the first lookback is covered if the framework delivers signal history before the view start). Forward source: same endpoint, refreshed daily. Please report per asset the first date, the number of days with one-day supply changes above 20 %, and whether Coin Metrics documents retroactive recomputation of SplyCur.","fields":["SplyCur"],"frequency":"1d"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 60-day abnormal return of the marked coins does not exceed the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or its gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism shape: the side-adjusted abnormal return is not larger at 60 days than at 21 days. A dilution drift must build steadily with the horizon; a peak at 5 days followed by a give-back means it is something else (a reversal or a news reaction).","Mechanism era: the latest third of dev has the wrong sign (K-0060). Then the pooled result counts as one boom episode, not a dilution premium.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5 or below the T-bill Sharpe + 0.10, or the one-sided bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference against T-bills not above zero.","Funding, not dilution: the book's return before costs and excluding funding (price P&L only) is not positive. Then any profit is funding received by the short leg, not the supply mechanism.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the lookback_days x hold_weeks neighbors (91/273 days, 13/39 weeks) beat the benchmark, or one third of dev carries more than 60 % of the log return.","Costs: at twice the modeled costs (including funding as charged) the net Sharpe no longer beats the benchmark."],"family":"new-listing-overhang","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":182},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Spot holders and leveraged perp longs who value coins by unit price and narrative and ignore the dilution of the unit (they look at the price chart, not at supply). On the other side are the issuance recipients who sell (miners, validators, farmers, treasuries). In perps the long side is speculators paying a funding rate set by leverage demand, not by the dilution of the underlying.","why":"New tokens enter circulation at a known, steady rate from protocol issuance: mining and staking rewards, liquidity-mining emissions, and treasury or ecosystem mints. A large part goes to recipients who are structural sellers. Miners and validators have fiat costs and taxes, yield farmers harvest and sell the reward token, and treasuries fund operations. The price therefore has to absorb a continuous supply flow, and holders who do not receive the issuance lose value at roughly the issuance rate. The equity analogue is net share issuance predicting lower returns (Pontiff and Woodgate 2008). In crypto the channel is more direct and much larger: annual supply growth runs from about 2 % for old proof-of-work coins to tens of percent for young emission-heavy tokens. The claim: over the following months, coins whose supply grew fastest over the last half year lag coins with the slowest supply growth and similar market beta, by a sizable fraction of the issuance gap.","why_not_arbitraged":"Harvesting the dilution needs a short. Spot shorting is scarce. Perp shorts on high-emission tokens face squeeze risk, high funding volatility and an 80-150 % volatility per coin, so the strategy is a slow, noisy, months-long premium with large tracking error: unattractive for desks that mark to market weekly. The cash-and-carry alternative (stake the spot, short the perp) needs capital on two venues and has unbonding lockups of days to weeks, slashing and custody risk. It is limited in size and does not cover emissions paid to non-stakers (farm rewards, treasury mints) at all. Supply data sits in on-chain analytics, not on trading screens."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"At each weekly formation (after the close that ends each Sunday UTC) on the eligible coins of the point-in-time top-40 perps: within each half split at the median 91-day beta to the equal-weight eligible universe, the floor(n_half/3) coins with the highest annualized supply growth over the last lookback_days (primary 182) are marked side -1, and the floor(n_half/3) coins with the lowest growth are marked side +1. The middle coins are the unmarked peers. Same eligibility and supply lag as the strategy. The mechanism says the -1 coins underperform and the +1 coins outperform the peers over the following months.","horizons":[5,21,42,60],"primary_horizon_days":60},"notes":"Brief fit: a long holding horizon in crypto. Each cohort is held 26 weeks (grid 13-39). The signal is a slow characteristic, so the book turns over little and a coin typically stays in its leg for many months. The mechanism test can only see the first 60 days of that hold (the judge's cap). The book is built from perps, because the short leg is essential and spot shorts carry no borrow cost in the engine.
Why the data is essential: no loadable dataset holds token supply. Listing age was used as a proxy in H-0058 and its lesson names 'listing age from token launch or unlock data is not loadable' as the open question. Coin Metrics Community is free, public, needs no key, covers 140+ assets daily and has a daily forward source, so the card could reach G5.
Family: reused new-listing-overhang on purpose. H-0058 ('token vesting overhang') filed the same economic claim, new supply reaching sellers depresses the price, under that family, so the trials should count together.
Why this is not a near-copy of H-0004, H-0058 or H-0082 (K-0107): (1) it measures supply growth directly instead of listing age; (2) it excludes coins with fewer than 91 days of perp history, so it is not a new-listing or launch-pump test; (3) it answers K-0107's and K-0074's demand to neutralize beta. Long and short legs are formed inside beta halves, with equal counts on each date, so the pooled side-adjusted event return is about half the long-minus-short spread of beta-matched coins, and generic market direction mostly cancels. The one known confound left is prior run-up. Prior returns are not matched, to keep the card to two parameters.
Expected size, written before any test: in liquid perps the supply growth of the top third is plausibly tens of percent a year and of the bottom third a few percent. If half of a 30-60 %/y issuance gap passes into relative price, the spread is 15-30 %/y. The book earns about half of it at gross 1 (0.5 per leg), so 7-15 %/y, against a residual volatility of a beta-matched 5-8-name-per-leg book of roughly 20-30 %/y. That gives an expected net Sharpe of about 0.3-0.7, so the absolute 0.5 floor is the likely strategy death. Per event, a 60-day side-adjusted gross of roughly 1.2-2.5 % against a perp round trip of about 0.3 % puts the cost ratio well above 1. The placebo bar is probably 2-4 % (60-day crypto windows, overlapping weekly formations, about 2.5 years of formations), so a 'cannot tell' near miss is likely unless the effect is at the top of this range (K-0034, K-0109).
Known risks: (a) Persistent characteristic: dilution is fairly persistent per coin, so the time-shifted placebo of the same coins absorbs part of a true premium (K-0025, H-0059). What the test can see is the time variation: emission launches and decays, halvings and burns move coins between legs. (b) Warm-up (K-0108): signal history before the view start is not delivered, so with lookback 182 the first formation comes about half a year into the perp panel. Formations then cover roughly two and a half years: about 130 weekly decision dates, enough for the 36-date and 30-event-date minimums, but a short sample (K-0006). (c) Funding: in boom phases short legs on speculative coins receive funding, which would flatter the book. Hence the price-only falsification line (H-0039 caution). (d) Survivorship: Coin Metrics coverage is chosen today. Dead coins are likely missing. They are more likely to be high-dilution tokens, so missing them biases against this card, not in its favour. (e) SplyCur counts minted supply. Tokens minted at genesis and released from vesting contracts show no change, so unlocks are invisible and the signal measures protocol issuance only. That dilutes the test but adds no look-ahead. (f) Possible retroactive recomputation by Coin Metrics, a K-0002-like risk: the Archivist is asked to report it. (g) Ticker mapping errors between Binance and Coin Metrics are possible: ambiguous tickers are dropped.
Benchmark: market-neutral, so T-bills with the absolute 0.5 Sharpe bar. Mean exposure is about 0.6-0.7 after the ramp and universe exits, and the rebalancing dates count as bets (exposure >= 0.5).","references":[{"cite":"Pontiff, Woodgate (2008) Share Issuance and Cross-Sectional Returns, Journal of Finance","year":2008}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: daily perp bars of binance_perp_1d (ret_co, ret_oc, close, quote_volume); daily current token supply per coin from the new dataset coinmetrics_supply_1d (Coin Metrics SplyCur, native units). Decision schedule: weekly, after the daily close (00:00 UTC) that ends each Sunday, trading at the next open. Universe on a decision day: the point-in-time top 40 perps of the judge's crypto_top_n universe. Eligible coins are universe members that meet all three of these conditions: (a) at least 91 daily perp returns in the last 91 days; (b) a supply value on the decision day and on the day lookback_days earlier (supply is read with a one-day lag: the value stamped on the day before the decision day); (c) no single-day absolute log change of supply above 0.20 inside the lookback window. This drops token migrations, redenominations and bridge-accounting jumps. The view starts at the perp panel start, so the first formation is lookback_days after the view start. Scores per eligible coin j: (1) dilution g_j = ln(S_j(t-1) / S_j(t-1-lookback_days)) * 365 / lookback_days; (2) beta_j = OLS slope of the coin's daily close-to-close log return on the equal-weight mean daily log return of the eligible coins, over the last 91 days. Cohort formation on each decision day, when at least 12 coins are eligible (otherwise no new cohort that week): split the eligible coins at the median beta into a low-beta half and a high-beta half (an odd coin goes to the high half). Within each half, rank by g_j. The floor(n_half/3) coins (at least 1) with the lowest g go to the long leg, and the floor(n_half/3) coins with the highest g go to the short leg. Ties are broken by instrument id. Inside the cohort, the long names together get +0.5 and the short names together get -0.5, equal weights within each leg (dollar-neutral, beta-matched by construction). Book: overlapping cohorts. Each cohort is held for hold_weeks weeks and enters the book with weight 1/hold_weeks. The target weight of a coin is the sum over the cohorts that are still active, so gross is at most 1. In the first hold_weeks weeks the book ramps up; the slots of cohorts not yet formed are cash. Weights of the active cohorts are fixed at formation (no drift rebalancing inside a cohort beyond what the engine applies to target weights). Leaving the universe: if a coin held by a cohort drops out of the point-in-time universe or has no bar, its weight in that cohort goes to zero at the next decision day (cash, not refilled), as the point-in-time universe rule demands (K-0051). It is not re-entered by that cohort. Missing data: a coin with no supply series is never eligible. The strategy must raise an error if the supply dataset is absent or entirely empty, instead of holding cash silently. Funding is charged by the engine (longs pay positive funding, shorts receive it). It is not part of the score.","params":{"hold_weeks":{"grid":[13,26,39],"value":26},"lookback_days":{"grid":[91,182,273],"value":182}},"timeframes":["1d","1w"]},"title":"Token supply dilution, beta-matched - top-40 Binance perps, short the fastest-growing token supply and long the slowest within beta halves, 26-week overlapping cohorts","universe":{"kind":"crypto_top_n","n":40}}

title: Net share repurchasers held for a year - LIQ-500 long-only, monthly overlapping 12-month cohorts of the top quintile of trailing net repurchase yield
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","tradable","listed","dollar_volume"],"frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"sharadar_sf1","fields":["sf1_art_ncfcommon","sf1_art_marketcap"],"frequency":"1q"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 60-session abnormal return of new top/bottom-quintile entries does not exceed the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the latest third of dev has the wrong sign (decay or no effect after publication, K-0060).","Mechanism shape: the 60-session abnormal return is not larger than the 21-session one (the claim is a slow drift, not a filing-week jump).","Net Sharpe of the primary book on dev below SPY total return Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference not above zero.","The book does not beat the 95th percentile of random-entry books drawn from eligible LIQ-500 stocks with the same turnover (the repurchase sort adds nothing over an equal-weight liquid-stock basket).","Fewer than 75 % of the neighbors (quantile 0.1 / 0.3, hold_months 6 / 18 and their combinations) beat SPY.","Post-publication (from 2008) excess Sharpe over SPY below half of the pre-publication excess.","S&P 500 alternative universe Sharpe below half the main Sharpe or below SPY; Sharpe at doubled costs below SPY."],"family":"trading-window-flows","holding_period":{"rebalance":"monthly","typical_days":365},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Investors who sell to the company in its buyback program and buyers of newly issued shares (offering allocations, shareholders of targets paid in stock, the market absorbing shares sold by employees after option exercise), plus cap-weighted index funds that mechanically buy new shares at float updates. They trade for reasons unrelated to the insider-information content of the issuance decision.","why":"Managers know more about the long-run value of their firm than outside investors and time equity transactions on it: they issue shares (seasoned offerings, stock-financed deals, option and stock-plan issuance) when the stock is rich and buy shares back when it is cheap. Investors under-react to the information in these transactions, because each one is small relative to market value, spread over many quarters and disclosed in the cash-flow statement rather than as news, so prices adjust slowly over the following one to three years (new-issues puzzle, buyback under-reaction, net issuance anomaly). A stock that becomes a large net repurchaser relative to its size should therefore beat other liquid stocks over the next year, and a stock that becomes a large net issuer should lag them.","why_not_arbitraged":"The effect is slow (it builds over years) and modest per year in large caps, so it pays only with long holding and patience; repurchasers are value-like and low-beta, so the tilt can lag a cap-weighted growth-led index for years (career and tracking-error risk for benchmarked managers); the short side (issuers) is concentrated in expensive growth names with squeeze risk and borrow cost, which keeps long/short arbitrageurs small."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"At a month-end decision date a LIQ-500 member newly enters the top quintile of trailing-twelve-month net repurchase yield (-ncfcommon / marketcap), having been outside it at the previous month-end: side +1 (should outperform the other members). A member newly entering the bottom quintile (heaviest net issuers): side -1 (should underperform).","horizons":[5,21,42,60],"primary_horizon_days":60},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks, cross-sectional, holding horizon 6-24 months (hold_months 6/12/18, overlapping monthly cohorts, value 12). Family: the sort variable (net equity issuance from the cash-flow statement) is essentially the net-repurchaser vs stock-compensation-issuer score of H-0019 and H-0027, so I file it under trading-window-flows so the trials count together, although the mechanism argued here is different (managerial market timing plus slow under-reaction, a year-long style drift, not a flow in the days after the trading window opens). This is the follow-up the Librarian asked for in H-0027 and K-0041: \"a low-turnover tilt on an always-invested book, argued as a style premium\". Honest snooping caveat: the lab already saw that the five-session versions built slowly with the horizon; the 60-session horizon and the 12-month hold are set by the literature (one-to-three-year drifts), not tuned on those results, and the grid is round values only. Why large caps: Fama and French (2008) report that the net-issues anomaly is pervasive across size groups including big stocks, unlike most other anomalies, so LIQ-500 is not the hopeless universe it was for the short-horizon cards. Expected size: a net-issuance spread of a few percent a year in big stocks gives roughly 0.4-0.8 % per side-adjusted event over 60 sessions; K-0109 put the placebo bar of a monthly sort with a quarter horizon near 0.46 %, so the mechanism test is a real test but could end in 'cannot tell'. Using new entries (not all quintile members) as events keeps the same-stock placebo from absorbing a persistent repurchaser state (the H-0059 trap); the price is fewer events (expected roughly 5-15 per side per month, about 3000 events on about 270 dates). Beta caveat (K-0074): repurchasers are lower-beta and issuers higher-beta than the peers, so in rising markets the raw side-adjusted return is biased against both sides; the test is conservative in the dev bull years. Strategy arithmetic: always invested (exposure about 1), about 270 monthly decision dates, each month a new cohort of about 100 names replaces the oldest, and because repurchase status is persistent the monthly one-way turnover should be well under 10 % of the book, so costs (3-6 bps half-spread tiers) are small and doubled costs should not matter. The benchmark is SPY total return: an equal-weight book of value-like repurchasers needs Sharpe about SPY + 0.10; my estimate is a book Sharpe 0.1-0.2 above SPY in dev, so the margin is thin, and the G2 random-entry null (equal-weight random liquid stocks) is the real test of the selection. The book holds only the long side; if the mechanism passes but the book fails the random-entry null, the effect lives in the issuer (short) side. Most likely deaths: placebo bar (sparse monthly dates), the latest third (growth-led 2014-2020 markets and post-publication decay), or the publication-decay check from 2008. No forward data for stocks, so G4 is the ceiling. RAM: two SF1 fields.","references":[{"cite":"Loughran, Ritter (1995) The New Issues Puzzle, Journal of Finance","year":1995},{"cite":"Ikenberry, Lakonishok, Vermaelen (1995) Market underreaction to open market share repurchases, Journal of Financial Economics","year":1995},{"cite":"Daniel, Titman (2006) Market Reactions to Tangible and Intangible Information, Journal of Finance","year":2006},{"cite":"Pontiff, Woodgate (2008) Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance","year":2008},{"cite":"Fama, French (2008) Dissecting Anomalies, Journal of Finance","year":2008}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: LIQ-500 point-in-time membership; Sharadar SF1 as-reported trailing-twelve-month fields sf1_art_ncfcommon (net cash flow from issuance (+) or purchase (-) of equity shares) and sf1_art_marketcap (market value frozen at the filing date), each usable from the day after its SEC filing as the loader provides them. Score: net repurchase yield NRY = -sf1_art_ncfcommon / sf1_art_marketcap (positive = net repurchaser). A stock is eligible on a decision date only if it is a LIQ-500 member and both fields are present (not NaN, loader staleness rule applies) with marketcap > 0; otherwise it is unranked. Decision dates: after the close of the last trading day of each month t. On each decision date rank eligible members by NRY (descending, ties broken by the instrument id order) and form cohort c_t = the top `quantile` fraction (rounded down, at least 1 name). Book: the live cohorts are those formed on the current and the previous hold_months - 1 decision dates (all formed cohorts while fewer than hold_months exist, so the book is fully invested from the first decision). Each live cohort gets an equal share of capital; inside a cohort the share is split equally across its names that are still LIQ-500 members and tradable on the decision date (names that left the universe or stopped trading are dropped from the cohort and their weight is spread over its remaining names; a cohort with no names left drops out and its share is spread over the other live cohorts). A stock in several live cohorts gets the sum of its weights. Target weights are set after the close of t and traded at the open of t + 1; between decision dates no trades, except that a stock that leaves the universe or delists is sold at the next possible open and the proceeds stay in cash until the next decision date. Long-only, gross <= 1, no shorts, no leverage. Event for the mechanism test (diagnostic.py): on each decision date, mask = True for a member that is in the top `quantile` of NRY now and was not in it at the previous decision date (side +1), and for a member that is in the bottom `quantile` of NRY now (heaviest net issuers) and was not in it at the previous decision date (side -1); on the first decision date no events.","params":{"hold_months":{"grid":[6,12,18],"value":12},"quantile":{"grid":[0.1,0.2,0.3],"value":0.2}},"timeframes":["1d","1mo","1q"]},"title":"Net share repurchasers held for a year - LIQ-500 long-only, monthly overlapping 12-month cohorts of the top quintile of trailing net repurchase yield","universe":{"kind":"liq_n","n":500}}

title: Bond-to-equity cross-asset momentum - 15 country ETFs, long where the local 10y bond rallied most over 12 months, short where it sold off most, 6-month cohorts
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_etf","macro"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","close_u","dollar_volume","tradable"],"frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"fred_oecd_10y_yields_1d","description":"NEW dataset, signal only, not tradable, delivered on the daily XNYS calendar as a step series (each monthly value stamped from its availability session on, see the point-in-time rule below). FRED (St. Louis Fed) series of the OECD Main Economic Indicators 'Interest Rates: Long-Term Government Bond Yields: 10-Year: Main (Including Benchmark)', monthly average, percent, not seasonally adjusted, free and public via fredgraph.csv: IRLTLT01USM156N (key US), IRLTLT01JPM156N (JP), IRLTLT01GBM156N (GB), IRLTLT01CAM156N (CA), IRLTLT01AUM156N (AU), IRLTLT01CHM156N (CH), IRLTLT01SEM156N (SE), IRLTLT01DEM156N (DE), IRLTLT01KRM156N (KR), IRLTLT01MXM156N (MX), IRLTLT01ZAM156N (ZA), IRLTLT01CLM156N (CL), IRLTLT01ILM156N (IL), IRLTLT01PLM156N (PL), IRLTLT01NZM156N (NZ). Point-in-time rule for ingest: stamp the value of month m on the first XNYS session of month m+2 (conservative for the OECD/FRED publication lag; FRED has no vintages for most of these). Please deliver from 1998-01 (or the series start, if later) and report the first valid month per key.","fields":["US","JP","GB","CA","AU","CH","SE","DE","KR","MX","ZA","CL","IL","PL","NZ"],"frequency":"1d"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the 60-session side-adjusted abnormal return of cohort members is below the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the side-adjusted mean in the latest third of dev is negative (kill condition even if the pooled test passes, K-0060).","Mechanism shape: the 60-session abnormal return is not larger than the 21-session one; slow rebalancing must build over months, a flat or front-loaded profile means this is not the claimed flow.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or below T-bill Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the difference to T-bills at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbors (lookback 9 and 15 months, hold 3 and 12 months and their combinations) beat the T-bill benchmark, or their median Sharpe is under 0.7 of the primary.","Concentration: one third of dev carries more than 60 % of the log return, or net Sharpe at doubled costs falls below the benchmark bar."],"family":"cross-asset-momentum","holding_period":{"rebalance":"monthly","typical_days":126},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Slow-rebalancing balanced investors who buy local equities months after the bond move instead of at once (they pay the drift), and equity-only investors who price country equities from equity-market information and ignore what the local bond market already priced.","why":"Pitkajarvi, Suominen and Vaittinen (2020, JFE) find in 20 countries that a country's past 12-month government bond return positively predicts its future equity market return, and attribute it to slow-moving capital: investors who hold both a country's bonds and its equities (home-biased pension funds, insurers, balanced and target-date funds with fixed strategic weights) rebalance slowly and in steps after a bond market shock. When local bonds rally (yields fall), the bond sleeve becomes overweight and the lower discount rate is priced first by rates investors; the cross-market investors move money into local equities over the following months (rebalancing bands, quarterly or annual committee cycles, liability reviews), so the local equity market drifts up relative to other countries. After a bond sell-off the same flow runs out of local equities. Because pension and insurance portfolios are strongly home-biased, the flow is country-specific, which is what a cross-section of country equity ETFs can isolate from the global factor.","why_not_arbitraged":"Exploiting it means a country-allocation spread with large tracking error, a Sharpe well under one and long losing stretches; equity and rates desks are separate mandates, and the capital that could arbitrage across the two markets is itself the slow-moving capital the mechanism describes (Duffie 2010). Mandates of the rebalancers (strategic weights, governance cycles) are not changed by the predictability."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"At each month-end decision date t, every instrument placed in the newly formed cohort: side +1 for the k countries with the highest vol-scaled 12-month local bond return proxy (largest yield fall), side -1 for the k with the lowest (largest yield rise), k = floor(N / 4) of the N eligible instruments, exactly as in the signal description (lookback 12 months, publication lag of the yields applied). The other eligible instruments are the unmarked peers (at least N - 2k >= 4 per date).","horizons":[5,21,42,60],"primary_horizon_days":60},"notes":"Brief: long horizon (6-24 months), cross-asset (signal from one market, trades in another, FRED allowed). The signal comes from each country's government bond market and the trade is in that country's equity ETF; the hold is six months of overlapping monthly cohorts (12 in the grid). The mechanism test horizon is capped at 60 sessions, so it sees only the first third of the hold; that is the closest fit the judge allows. WHY A NEW DATASET: the mechanism is country-specific (local bond move -> local equity flow), so it needs one bond market per equity market. The catalog has only US yields (fred_macro DGS10/DGS2), and international bond ETFs start after 2007 and are multi-country baskets. The FRED/OECD monthly series are free, public, one source and one format for all 15 countries (all ids checked to exist on FRED). Monthly averages are enough for a 12-month signal; the two-month stamping lag gives up a little freshness to remove publication look-ahead. UNIVERSE RULE (not picked on performance): the US (SPY) plus every country with a US-listed iShares MSCI single-country ETF launched by 2010 that has its own floating currency and monetary policy and an OECD 10-year yield series on FRED. Euro-area members share one policy rate and their yields co-moved closely for much of the sample, so ranking them separately would put several near-identical signals in one leg; Germany (EWG) represents the euro area. Pegged or managed currencies (Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan, China) and countries without a FRED OECD 10-year series (Brazil, Turkey, Thailand, Indonesia, Peru) are out by the rule. Ten instruments are eligible from about 2000-2001 (KR and MX once their yield histories allow), 15 by 2011. Signal history before the view start is not delivered (K-0108), so the first cohort needs about 26 months of yields from 1998-01 (24 monthly changes for s_i plus the lag); I expect the first cohort around 2000-04. WHAT IS NEW vs the dead ideas: H-0060 sorted countries on their own multi-year equity return (reversal) and H-0056 timed SPY on oil; H-0061 timed SPY vs IEF on a credit spread; the mrel scan and K-0080 cover daily lead-lag. Here the signal is another asset class of the same country over 12 months, the horizon is months, and the trade is cross-sectional across countries with both sides marked, so the placebo mean should be near zero and the global equity factor cancels. Not SPY/IEF, not a binary switch (K-0005). Study 2 used each class's own trend; this is a cross-asset signal. Family cross-asset-momentum is new; if the Chair thinks it belongs to an existing cross-market information family I accept the merge. CONFOUNDS I EXPECT (stated so the result can be read): (1) currency: ETF returns are in USD while the paper uses local or hedged equity returns; a local yield fall often comes with rate cuts and a weaker currency over the following months (lower carry), which works against the long leg. A failure with a flat or wrong sign would then say 'not harvestable through unhedged ETFs', not 'the paper is wrong'. (2) beta (K-0074): vol-scaling keeps high-volatility emerging yields from sitting in the legs by construction, so the average beta gap between legs should be small, but in global risk-off emerging-market yields tend to rise and core yields fall, so the book can be short high-beta countries after stress; a stress-continuation reading is possible and the judge has no beta-adjusted abnormal return. NUMBERS (forecast, before any data): about 228 formation dates in dev with 4-6 marked instruments each, so about 1000-1300 events on about 228 dates, 4 or more unmarked peers per date. I expect a gross side-adjusted abnormal return of about 0.6-1.2 % per event at 60 sessions (a country spread of roughly 3-5 % a year); per-event 60-session noise is about 5 %, and with overlapping windows the placebo bar is probably around 0.5-0.8 %, so the test can tell if the effect is at the middle of my range and is a coin flip at the low end. Round-trip cost for these ETFs is roughly 0.1-0.5 % (EIS, EPOL, ENZL, ECH, EZA in higher tiers), so the cost ratio should not bind. Book: gross 1, dollar-neutral, mean exposure about 0.95 (ramp-up over the first H months), about 250 monthly rebalances, turnover about 1/H of the book per month (about 0.5 % a year of cost). Expected net Sharpe 0.3-0.6 against a floor of 0.5: the absolute floor is the most likely strategy death, and I file the card anyway because the mechanism test is the informative, cheap part and the lab has never tested cross-asset momentum. The second most likely death is G2 sub-period concentration (few global rate cycles). ETFs and OECD yields have no forward source here, so G4 is the ceiling. Publication: the reference year is the end of dev, so there is no post-publication part in dev; the holdout is the only post-publication check.","references":[{"cite":"Pitkajarvi, Suominen, Vaittinen (2020) Cross-asset signals and time series momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 136(1)","year":2020},{"cite":"Duffie (2010) Presidential Address: Asset Price Dynamics with Slow-Moving Capital, Journal of Finance","year":2010}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: daily total returns of the 15 ETFs (sharadar_sfp) and, per country, the OECD monthly-average 10-year government bond yield from the new dataset fred_oecd_10y_yields_1d (a daily step series of the monthly values; key per country: US for SPY, JP for EWJ, GB for EWU, CA for EWC, AU for EWA, CH for EWL, SE for EWD, DE for EWG, KR for EWY, MX for EWW, ZA for EZA, CL for ECH, IL for EIS, PL for EPOL, NZ for ENZL). A monthly yield value is usable only from the first XNYS session of the second calendar month after the month it averages (the value for month m from the first session of month m+2), which covers the OECD/FRED publication lag; the strategy always uses the latest usable value, never anything later. Decision dates: after the close of the last XNYS session of each calendar month (t); trades at the open of the next session. Score at t for country i: let y_i(0) be the latest usable monthly yield at t and y_i(-L) the usable monthly yield L months before it (L = lookback_months). dy_i = y_i(0) - y_i(-L) in percentage points. s_i = standard deviation of the month-over-month changes of y_i over the 36 usable months ending at y_i(0) (at least 24 changes required) times sqrt(L). score_i = -dy_i / s_i (a vol-scaled local bond return proxy: positive when the local bond market rallied). Eligibility at t: the ETF has a price bar on t and at least 63 sessions of history, and score_i exists. If fewer than 8 instruments are eligible, no new cohort is formed at t (the existing cohorts are kept). Cohort at t: with N eligible instruments let k = floor(N / 4). Long the k highest scores, short the k lowest (ties broken by the larger absolute score magnitude, then alphabetically by ticker). Within each leg weights are proportional to 1 / sigma_i, sigma_i = standard deviation of daily log total returns over the last 63 sessions, normalized so the long leg sums to +0.5 / H and the short leg to -0.5 / H (H = hold_months). Book: the target weight of each ETF is the sum of its weights in the H most recent cohorts (a cohort formed at month-end t is held through the next H month-end rebalances and dropped at the H-th one). Gross exposure is therefore at most 1 and dollar-neutral. Weights are reset to the target only at month-end rebalances. Missing data: an ETF without a price bar on a rebalance day gets target weight 0 in every cohort from that day on; a missing yield month makes the country ineligible for new cohorts until both yields and 24 changes exist again (no filling, no interpolation). Instruments listed later (EZA, ECH, EIS, EPOL, ENZL) enter only through the eligibility rule.","params":{"hold_months":{"grid":[3,6,12],"value":6},"lookback_months":{"grid":[9,12,15],"value":12}},"timeframes":["1d","1mo"]},"title":"Bond-to-equity cross-asset momentum - 15 country ETFs, long where the local 10y bond rallied most over 12 months, short where it sold off most, 6-month cohorts","universe":{"instruments":["SPY","EWJ","EWU","EWC","EWA","EWL","EWD","EWG","EWY","EWW","EZA","ECH","EIS","EPOL","ENZL"],"kind":"instruments"}}

title: Currency value into country equity ETFs - long the 2 cheapest, short the 2 richest of 10 developed currencies vs 5-year average spot, 12-month cohorts
card_json:
{"asset_classes":["us_etf","fx"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","close_u","tradable"],"frequency":"1d","period":["1998-01-02","2026-09-25"]},{"dataset":"fred_macro","description":"FRED daily noon spot rates of ten developed-market currencies against the USD; signal only, not tradable.","fields":["DEXUSAL","DEXCAUS","DEXSDUS","DEXJPUS","DEXSZUS","DEXSIUS","DEXUSUK","DEXUSEU","DEXNOUS","DEXUSNZ"],"frequency":"1d","period":["1998-01-02","2026-09-25"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 60-session abnormal return of the marked country ETFs is not above the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism sign: the side-adjusted abnormal return is negative in 2 of the 3 dev blocks, or negative in the latest third of dev (decay or regime, K-0060): either kills the card.","Mechanism shape: the mean side-adjusted abnormal return at 60 sessions is not larger than at 21 sessions. A value effect must build with the horizon; an effect concentrated in the first weeks is reversal or noise, not the currency anchor.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or below the T-bill Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference to T-bills at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbors (lookback 36/84, n_per_leg 1/3, hold 6/18 and their combinations) beat the T-bill benchmark, or Sharpe at doubled costs below the benchmark.","Concentration: one dev third carries more than 60 % of the log return, or fewer than 2 of 3 thirds beat T-bills."],"family":"long-term-reversal","holding_period":{"rebalance":"monthly","typical_days":252},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"US investors in country funds who allocate on trailing USD returns (country-fund flows chase past performance, and a currency slide makes the trailing USD return of a country look bad), and global equity managers benchmarked in USD who cut exposure to markets whose currency has weakened, together with home-biased local investors who do not price the competitiveness gain until it shows in reported earnings.","why":"A developed-market currency that trades far below its own multi-year average USD price tends to recover over the following one to three years (purchasing-power anchor; currency value, Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf 2017; the lab saw the same in G10 currency trusts, H-0062). An unhedged US-listed country equity ETF carries that currency one for one, so the currency recovery lands in its USD return. A second channel runs through the real economy: a cheap currency raises the local-currency profits of the country's exporters and multinationals with a lag of several quarters (pricing-to-market, translation of foreign sales), which a market anchored on trailing earnings prices slowly. Both channels say the same thing for a USD investor: the country ETFs whose currency is cheap against its own history should beat those whose currency is rich, over months to years. The signal lives in the FX market (FRED noon spot rates); the trade lives in equity ETFs.","why_not_arbitraged":"The payoff takes one to three years and comes with currency and equity risk at the same time; a value bet against the trend can lose for years (career risk, mandate limits on tracking error), currency value has no carry to pay for the wait among low-inflation developed currencies, and arbitrage capital in country allocation is small next to benchmark-hugging global equity money."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"At each monthly decision date (after the close of the last XNYS session of the month), a country ETF whose currency is among the 2 cheapest of the eligible countries by the 60-month value score V_c (side +1), or among the 2 richest (side -1). The other eligible country ETFs on that date are the unmarked peers. Events are marked only on dates with at least 7 eligible countries (4 marked + at least 3 unmarked peers); with lookback 60 this holds on every decision date from the first one (seven countries eligible from about 2003-01), so no strategy date is missing from the event study.","horizons":[5,21,42,60],"primary_horizon_days":60},"notes":"Brief fit: cross-asset (signal from the FX market via FRED, trade in US-listed equity ETFs), holding 12 months in overlapping monthly cohorts (inside the 6-24 month brief; neighbors 6 and 18). The judge caps the mechanism horizon at 60 sessions, so G1 sees only the first quarter of a 12-month claim; that is why the shape criterion (60 > 21) is part of the card.
Relation to earlier cards. H-0062 (same family, long-term-reversal) traded the currency value score in six G10 currency trusts and passed the mechanism test, then missed the absolute Sharpe floor. H-0060 (same family) sorted country equity ETFs on their own 48-month USD return and found no reversal (wrong sign early). K-0073 left the split open: currency value works, equity-return reversal does not, and USD country ETFs carry both. This card asks the question that sits between them: does the currency anchor, measured only in the FX market, predict the USD return of the equity vehicle? It is not the H-0060 score (a country whose equity soared while its currency slid is cheap here and a winner there), and not the H-0062 book (equity ETFs instead of trusts, ten countries instead of six: adds SEK, SGD, NOK, NZD; no currency trusts traded). The signal formula is the H-0062 score by design, so the family and its trial count are shared on purpose. Either verdict is informative: a pass says the FX value effect survives, and is perhaps reinforced by the competitiveness channel, inside liquid equity wrappers; a failure next to H-0062's pass says the local equity leg offsets the currency recovery (a cheap currency marks a local slump that persists).
Anchor and carry (K-0073). The anchor is the nominal 5-year average spot. The universe is restricted on purpose to developed, low-inflation currencies (no BRL, MXN, INR, KRW, CNY), where inflation gaps over five years are small, so the nominal score is close to a real one and does not turn into a permanent long on high-inflation, high-carry currencies. A residual carry tilt remains (AUD, NZD, NOK had higher rates than JPY, CHF for much of the sample); interest-rate data per country are not loadable, so this is stated, not removed. Because value scores cycle over a few years, the time-shifted placebo reshuffles which countries are marked; a static carry or country premium would show up in the placebo mean (K-0025), not in the percentile.
Beta caveat (K-0074). The G1 abnormal return is raw against the unmarked country ETFs. Cheap currencies are often commodity or risk-on currencies after a slump (higher equity beta), rich ones often havens (JPY, CHF, lower beta), so the long leg may carry more world-equity beta than the short leg. Both legs are marked and the side alternates as currencies cycle, which limits but does not remove this. The Builder should report the mean trailing beta of the long and short legs to the equal-weight country set, and the by-side result, if the gate output allows.
Data and timing. Both datasets start 1998-01-02 so the signal history is delivered from the view start (K-0108). FRED euro starts 1999-01, so with lookback 60 the first decision with a value score is about 2003-01 (seven countries; EZU from about 2004-01; ENZL and NORW listed late 2010, eligible from then since their currency windows are already full). Neighbor lookback 84 starts about 2005. FRED FX are New York noon fixings, stale for Asian hours (catalog), irrelevant at a multi-year anchor and a monthly decision. Instruments: EWA, EWC, EWD, EWJ, EWL, EWS, EWU from the 1990s, EZU from 2000; NORW and ENZL from late 2010. If any ticker is missing in SFP, G0 should fail loudly (K-0102), not drop the country silently.
Expected counts and size (K-0069, K-0098, K-0034). Event dates: about 213 monthly dates in 2003-2020 with a 60-session forward window; marked events 4 per date, about 850 in total; unmarked peers per date: 3 (2003), 4 (2004-2010), 6 (2011 on). The book is invested from the first cohort and near gross 1 after the first year (mean exposure about 0.85-0.95 over dev, dollar-neutral); about 216 decision dates; turnover is 1/12 of the book per month, so costs (liquid iShares country ETFs, tier spread) are a few bps per year and survive x2. My own forecast of the placebo bar at 60 sessions: country-ETF relative returns over 60 sessions have a standard deviation of about 7-8 %, about 70 effective independent dates after overlap, so the bar is roughly 0.8 % per side-adjusted event. The currency channel alone, at the size H-0062 saw, would give roughly 0.5-1 % per event at 60 sessions, near that bar; the card passes the mechanism test only if the equity channel adds to the currency recovery rather than offsetting it. Gross per event should be several times the round-trip cost of liquid country ETFs (roughly 10-20 bps), so the cost check is not expected to bind.
Most likely death: the strategy gate. A dollar-neutral 2-versus-2 country book has a volatility of roughly 10-12 %, so it needs about 5-6 % a year to reach the absolute Sharpe floor of 0.5; the currency channel alone gives perhaps half of that. A mechanism pass with a strategy failure would still settle K-0073's open question. ETFs have no forward data, so G4 is the ceiling. No dates, episodes or instruments were chosen from hindsight: the universe is every developed-market country ETF in the catalog's issuer families whose currency has a FRED daily rate in the lab's fred_macro dataset (Hong Kong is pegged and has no FRED series here; Denmark, Israel, Taiwan and South Africa have no series in fred_macro).","references":[{"cite":"Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf (2017) Currency Value, Review of Financial Studies","year":2017},{"cite":"Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen (2013) Value and Momentum Everywhere, Journal of Finance","year":2013}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: daily FRED noon spot rates of ten currencies against the USD (fred_macro, clock next_morning, so the value of day d is used from day d+1) and the ten country ETFs. Mapping ETF -> series -> USD price P of one unit of the foreign currency: EWA -> DEXUSAL (P = x); EWC -> DEXCAUS (P = 1/x); EWD -> DEXSDUS (P = 1/x); EWJ -> DEXJPUS (P = 1/x); EWL -> DEXSZUS (P = 1/x); EWS -> DEXSIUS (P = 1/x); EWU -> DEXUSUK (P = x); EZU -> DEXUSEU (P = x); NORW -> DEXNOUS (P = 1/x); ENZL -> DEXUSNZ (P = x). Decision dates: after the close of the last XNYS session of each month (day t); orders fill at the open of day t+1. Value score of country c on day t: V_c = mean of ln P_c over the FX observations available at t inside the last lookback_months x 21 XNYS sessions, minus ln P_c of the latest observation available at t. V_c > 0 means the currency is cheap against its own average. A country is eligible on day t only if (a) at least 80 % of the sessions in the window have an FX observation and the latest observation is at most 10 sessions old, and (b) its ETF has a tradable bar on day t (so ENZL and NORW enter only once listed and once their window is filled; EZU waits for a full euro window). Ranking: sort eligible countries by V_c; the n_per_leg highest (cheapest currencies) form the long leg, the n_per_leg lowest (richest) the short leg. If fewer than 2 x n_per_leg + 1 countries are eligible, no cohort is formed that month (that cohort stays in cash). Book: overlapping cohorts. Each month a new cohort is formed with weight 1 / hold_months; inside a cohort each long name gets +0.5 / n_per_leg and each short name -0.5 / n_per_leg of the cohort weight (dollar-neutral, cohort gross 1). A cohort is held unchanged for hold_months monthly decisions, then dropped. The target weight of each ETF is the sum over the live cohorts (long and short slots of the same ETF net out); gross therefore never exceeds 1. If an ETF stops having a tradable bar, its slots in every live cohort go to cash until those cohorts expire; no other name replaces it. Targets are set only on decision dates (monthly); no intra-month trading. Missing FX values are never filled forward beyond the 10-session staleness rule.","params":{"hold_months":{"grid":[6,12,18],"value":12},"lookback_months":{"grid":[36,60,84],"value":60},"n_per_leg":{"grid":[1,2,3],"value":2}},"timeframes":["1d","1mo"]},"title":"Currency value into country equity ETFs - long the 2 cheapest, short the 2 richest of 10 developed currencies vs 5-year average spot, 12-month cohorts","universe":{"instruments":["EWA","EWC","EWD","EWJ","EWL","EWS","EWU","EZU","NORW","ENZL"],"kind":"instruments"}}

title: Absorbed taker flow on Binance perps - after an hour of extreme one-sided taker volume that failed to move the price, trade with the passive absorber, both sides, hold 6 hours
card_json:
{"asset_classes":["crypto_perp"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"binance_perp_15m","description":"o h l c, qv, tbq, real and universe flags of the PIT top-20 Binance USD-M perps; funding is charged by the engine. Dev 2020-2022 only.","frequency":"15m"}],"falsification_criteria":["Fewer than 300 trades in the 2020-2022 dev period at the primary configuration: absorption hours of this kind are too rare to be a strategy.","Net Sharpe below 0.5 on dev, or the bootstrap bound of the mean net trade not above zero (G1).","Mechanism-level: Sharpe with a one-candle later fill below 50 % of the primary Sharpe. The card claims the price has not yet moved when the event is seen, so the edge must not be front-loaded; failing this puts the card with K-0077 (taker moves consumed within a candle) and refutes the absorption reading.","Net Sharpe at doubled costs not positive.","Fewer than 2 of 3 dev sub-periods positive, more than 60 % of profit in one third, or the latest third of dev negative (K-0060 decay stated as a kill condition).","Neighbours of imbalance_z (2.0, 3.0) or hold_candles (12, 48): fewer than 75 % positive or median Sharpe below 70 % of the primary.","The same trades placed at random times do not beat the 95th percentile of the random-entry null.","Mechanism control (Builder diagnostic, reported in the build log): the mirror event set (same imbalance and volume conditions but s * R_t > 0, i.e. the flow DID move the price) traded the same way (against the flow) must earn less gross per trade than the absorption set. If absorption events earn no more than flow-driven events, the edge is generic reversal against taker flow (short-term-reversal family, H-0035), not absorption.","Mechanism control: if the long side (absorbed selling) and the short side (absorbed buying) have mean gross trades of opposite sign, the symmetric absorption claim is false and any profit is market drift in one direction."],"family":"taker-flow-absorption","holding_period":{"rebalance":"event","typical_days":0.25},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"The aggressive takers of the absorbed hour and their followers: leveraged traders whose market orders or stop/liquidation orders hit a wall of resting liquidity, and short-horizon momentum traders who read heavy taker buying (selling) as bullish (bearish) and keep paying the spread in that direction. They lose the spread plus the subsequent move in the absorber's direction.","why":"In a limit-order market an aggressive (taker) order flow normally moves the price in its own direction; that is why taker imbalance explains contemporaneous returns so well. When an hour of unusually one-sided, high-volume taker flow leaves the price unchanged or moved against the flow, someone resting passive orders absorbed it: a large patient trader (a fund or market maker working a big order with limit orders, an arbitrageur hedging a spot or cross-venue position, an OTC desk unwinding inventory) whose demand exceeds the aggressive supply at that price. Two things follow. (1) The absorber is still there and still has size to do, so the price drifts in the absorber's direction over the next hours once the aggressive side stops. (2) The aggressive side (stop and liquidation orders, momentum chasers, traders who pay the spread to get out) has spent its ammunition without moving the price and, if leveraged, is now on the wrong side of a level that held, so its exits add to the move. The strategy enters only after the absorption is visible in a closed hour and the price has NOT yet moved in the absorber's direction, so, unlike the taker-move cards of K-0077 (H-0035, H-0063), the payoff is not front-loaded into the signal candle: the information (hidden passive demand) is not yet in the price.","why_not_arbitraged":"Exchange data feeds show taker volume and price, but not who rests the passive size; inferring an absorber from hourly flow is noisy, the effect is small per hour relative to crypto volatility, and it sits in mid-cap perps where a fast desk's capacity is limited and taker costs are high. Large absorbers deliberately hide size (iceberg-like slicing), and the obvious public reading of heavy taker flow is the opposite one (follow the aggressors), so the crowd trades against this signal rather than with it. Capacity is a few hundred thousand dollars per event at most."},"notes":"Brief: SCALPING on binance_perp_15m, holding a few hours; no mechanism_test (intraday judge has none).
Why this is not a near-copy of earlier intraday cards. H-0035 faded hours with a 4-sigma PRICE move on taker- dominated volume (liquidity provision after an overshoot); H-0063 followed taker-dominated breakouts; both selected candles in which the aggressive flow had already moved the price, and both lost the edge to a one-candle delay (K-0077). This card requires the opposite: extreme taker imbalance with NO price move in its direction. The claim is about hidden passive demand that has not yet reached the price, not about a price overshoot reverting, so the family is a new mechanism (taker-flow-absorption), not short-term-reversal. I flag the overlap honestly: both this card and H-0035 end up trading against the aggressive side, and if the Chair judges that the same mechanism the family should be merged into short-term-reversal (stricter penalty, which I accept). The mirror control in the falsification criteria is meant to settle exactly that question. Not tested in study 16 (ORB, funding extreme, BTC lead-lag, CME gap, squeeze, pullback, shock, range) or study 15 (price-structure triggers).
Related literature (not cited in references because it is not the source of this claim and does not test it): Kitron and Wengrowicz (2026, arXiv 2608.21888) report that 15-minute crypto reversal concentrates after moves driven by aggressive taker flow, i.e. the flow-driven set; this card trades the complementary flow-opposed set at a much longer horizon. Kim and Hansen (2026, arXiv 2607.09426) show taker imbalance at quarter-hour boundaries forecasts 4-12 hour returns in Binance perps, but with a gross far below cost when traded every quarter hour, which is why this card trades only rare, extreme, high-volume hours.
Costs and expected gross (K-0077 asks for the gross after a one-candle delay). Top-20 perps in 2020-2022 sit mostly in the 1.5-6 bps slippage tiers, so a round trip costs about 13-22 bps and 26-44 bps at doubled costs. The card needs a mean gross of roughly 45 bps or more per trade over 6 hours to survive doubled costs, about 0.2 standard deviations of a 6-hour alt return; I expect the delayed fill to lose little because the price has not moved at the signal. Honest prior: the gross may well be 20-30 bps, in which case it dies on doubled costs like H-0035.
Choices fixed in advance, not tuned: one-hour window (the lab's hourly feature scale), 30-day baseline, volume at least 2x its 30-day mean, return condition at exactly zero (no tolerance band), five equal slots. Only the imbalance threshold and the hold are on the grid (9 configurations). Trade count is the main design risk: conditions (a)-(c) are jointly rare; my rough estimate is several hundred to about 1500 trades in dev at the primary, and the 3.0 neighbour will have fewer. Events cluster in market-wide flush hours; the slot ranking and the no-pyramiding rule limit that clustering. A sustained crash (2022) is where absorbers can be overrun; the latest-third criterion will show it.
Why most likely to die: doubled costs (thin per-trade gross on alts), or the latest third of dev (K-0060). An informative death: if the one-candle delay kills it, absorption is just another front-loaded taker effect; if the mirror control earns as much, it is generic reversal.","signal":{"description":"Data: binance_perp_15m candles of the point-in-time top-20 perps by 30-day quote volume (the judge's crypto_top_n universe). Decisions are taken after the close of every 15-minute candle t using data up to and including candle t; fills at the open of candle t+1 (engine default).
1. Hourly window. For every symbol and every candle t, take the last 4 candles t-3..t (one hour). QV_t = sum of qv over the 4 candles, TB_t = sum of tbq over the 4 candles, imbalance I_t = 2*TB_t/QV_t - 1 (in [-1, 1]; positive = takers bought). R_t = c_t / c_(t-4) - 1 (close four candles back to close of t).
2. Baselines (strictly past, no overlap with the window): mu_I and sd_I = mean and standard deviation of I over the 2880 candles (30 days) ending at candle t-4; QVbar = mean of QV (the rolling 4-candle sum) over the same 2880 candles. A symbol needs at least 2400 real candles (real == True) in that baseline and all 4 window candles real with qv > 0; otherwise no event. z_t = (I_t - mu_I) / sd_I.
3. Event (absorption) at candle t for symbol j, all three conditions:
  (a) |z_t| >= k (parameter imbalance_z);
  (b) QV_t >= 2 * QVbar (fixed, not a parameter: the hour carried real size);
  (c) s * R_t <= 0 with s = sign(z_t): the hour's close-to-close return was zero or went AGAINST the aggressive
      flow (taker buying with a flat or falling price, or taker selling with a flat or rising price).
Side = -s: long after absorbed taker selling, short after absorbed taker buying.
4. Positions. Five slots of 0.20 of equity each (gross <= 1). On an event, if the symbol has no open position and a slot is free, open the position at the open of t+1 with weight 0.20 * side. If more events than free slots occur at the same decision, take them in order of |z_t| (largest first); the rest are dropped, not queued. A symbol with an open position ignores new events (no pyramiding, no reversal) until it is closed.
5. Exit. Close at the open of candle t+1+H, i.e. after H candles (parameter hold_candles). Exit tolerant of the universe rule (K-0051): if the symbol leaves the point-in-time universe or its candle is not real before the scheduled exit, close at the first decision at which that happens. No stop-loss, no profit target. Funding is charged by the engine on positions open at settlement.
6. Nothing else: no trend or regime filter, no BTC leader, no funding condition. Symbols not yet listed or without 30 days of history cannot produce events.","params":{"hold_candles":{"grid":[12,24,48],"value":24},"imbalance_z":{"grid":[2.0,2.5,3.0],"value":2.5}},"timeframes":["15m","1h"]},"title":"Absorbed taker flow on Binance perps - after an hour of extreme one-sided taker volume that failed to move the price, trade with the passive absorber, both sides, hold 6 hours","universe":{"kind":"crypto_top_n","n":20}}

Frazzini finds that stocks with large unrealized gains underreact only to positive news and stocks with large unrealized losses only to negative news, so post-news drift is largest when news and overhang have the same sign. Among stocks with a large earnings release reaction, high-overhang stocks should therefore beat low-overhang stocks in the following week: with good news because the gain stocks keep drifting up while the loss stocks do not, with bad news because the loss stocks keep drifting down while the gain stocks do not. The brief (US single stocks, 1-5 day hold, cross-sectional) fits directly. RELATION TO OTHER FAMILIES, stated so the Chair can count trials. The events are a subset of the release-reaction events of the post-earnings-announcement-drift family (H-0028, H-0031, H-0033), but the side is set by the overhang, not by the news sign: long and short legs both contain good-news and bad-news stocks, so a generic drift that does not depend on the overhang cancels (exactly when the four cells are balanced, roughly otherwise). Builder: check on a few stocks that ARQ ncfo is the quarter's own value and not fiscal year-to-date; if it is year-to-date, use the quarter's increment within the fiscal year and say so.","fields":["sf1_arq_netinc","sf1_arq_ncfo","sf1_arq_assets"],"frequency":"1q","period":["1998-01-02","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return after entry is at or below the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or below the round-trip cost per event: no exploitable accrual adjustment after the filing in LIQ-500.","Mechanism shape: if the 1- and 3-session abnormal returns are about zero or wrong-signed and the effect appears only at 10-21 sessions, the filing-information claim is wrong (it is the slow always-on accrual style of H-0032), even if the pooled 5-session test passes.","Mechanism decay: the latest third of dev (about 2013-2020) has the wrong sign: the anomaly is gone (Green, Hand and Soliman's demise reading) and the card is dead regardless of the pooled result.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5 or the bootstrap bound of Sharpe minus T-bill at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbors (leg_quantile 0.1/0.3, hold_days 3/8) clear the T-bill bar, or doubled costs leave Sharpe below the bar."],"family":"anomalies-at-earnings-news","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Earnings-fixated holders and momentum or earnings-surprise traders who bought the headline number at the release and do not re-read the filed cash-flow statement; they hold or keep buying high-accrual firms and under-buy low-accrual firms in the days after the filing.","why":"Earnings fixation (Sloan 1996): investors price the headline earnings number and underweight how much of it is backed by operating cash flow, so firms whose earnings are mostly accruals are overpriced relative to firms whose earnings are mostly cash. For a large share of firms the full cash-flow statement, and with it the accrual component of the quarter, becomes public only with the 10-Q or 10-K filing, which often comes days or weeks after the earnings press release. Balsam, Bartov and Marquardt (2002) find that prices react to the quarter's unexpected accruals around the 10-Q filing date, and that the reaction is slower where the investor base is less sophisticated. The claim of this card is that the price adjustment to the newly filed accrual is not finished by the session after the filing becomes usable: low-accrual filers keep beating high-accrual filers over the following week. The event is the arrival of the accrual information itself, not a later earnings release that resolves an old anomaly.","why_not_arbitraged":"Each signal is small per name, appears on scattered dates through a seven-week filing season, needs parsing of the filed statements, and pays only a fraction of a percent over a week against the idiosyncratic risk of single names; shorting high-accrual growth names carries squeeze and borrow risk. Sophisticated traders take the first sessions (which this card does not try to capture, see notes), and capacity for the slower remainder is limited by the spread cost of a week-long single-name book."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"A LIQ-500 stock's new 10-Q/10-K filing becomes usable on session t (the as-reported quarterly net income, operating cash flow and assets change, first change in 40 sessions) and its quarterly accruals (net income minus operating cash flow, over assets) fall in the bottom leg_quantile (side +1) or the top leg_quantile (side -1) of the current LIQ-500 cross-section of latest accruals.","horizons":[1,3,5,10,21],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks, LIQ-500, cross-sectional, 5-session hold, mechanism test declared. Why this is not a retry of H-0032 (anomalies-at-earnings-news, accruals-profitability-asset-growth composite in a window around the predicted 8-K release, failed with a slow shape): that card assumed an old anomaly is corrected at the next earnings news; this card times the trade to the arrival of the accrual number itself (the SEC filing, real filing date from SF1, no date prediction) and uses accruals alone. Filed in the same family on purpose, so the trials count together. Why it is worth one trial: H-0019 passed its mechanism test clearly when anchored to the filing and failed when moved to the release (H-0027), and its sort (repurchases, stock issuance) is also cash-flow-statement information; K-0110 left open whether that pass was filing-linked news. This card tests the filing-news reading with the canonical cash-flow-statement signal. If it fails with a flat first week, filing-anchored information in LIQ-500 is closed; if it passes with a front-loaded shape, H-0019 was news, not flow. Timing: SF1 values are usable from the session after the SEC filing date, so with a decision at that close the entry is two sessions after the filing. The filing-window reaction of Balsam et al. is therefore NOT harvested; only the slower remainder is tested. The same-stock time-shifted placebo absorbs the always-on level of a stock's accruals (K-0025), so the test asks exactly whether the week after the filing is special. Forecasts (K-0098, K-0120): about 500 members x 4 filings x 85-90 % SF1 coverage = 1700-1800 filing events per year, 40 % in the two legs = about 700 events per year, roughly 14,000-16,000 events on 3,000-4,000 dates over 1998-2020 (fewer in the 63-session warm-up and if ARQ coverage is thinner early). Clustered in filing seasons (about weeks 3-10 after each quarter end, plus off-calendar fiscal years). Mean open positions about 700 x 5 / 252 = 14, gross about 14 x 0.04 = 0.55, capped at 1.0 at season peaks; mean exposure forecast 0.4-0.55. Round trip per event leg: half-spread 3-6 bps by rank (x2.5 before 2001-04), so about 8-12 bps after decimalization and 20-30 bps before; pooled roughly 12-15 bps. Expected gross per event at 5 sessions: an annual accrual spread of 5-8 % in large caps spread evenly would give only about 5-8 bps per event-side, under cost; the card needs the filing week to carry two to three times its share (15-25 bps) to clear cost. Book: at 15-20 bps net per event x 700 events x 0.04 = 4-6 %/yr against a vol of roughly 5 %, a Sharpe near the 0.5 floor. Most likely deaths, in order: decay in the latest third (accrual anomaly reported to fade after the early 2000s, and more firms now put the cash-flow statement in the press release, so less is new at the filing); gross under cost; strategy under the absolute Sharpe floor. Biases against the card: high-accrual firms lean to growth and higher beta (K-0074), so bull years favour the short leg; high accruals often come with an earnings beat whose release drift (K-0046) also favours the short leg. Quarterly accruals have industry seasonality; firms in the same filing season mostly share the fiscal quarter, which limits it. Banks and insurers have accruals that mean little; the universe is ticker-blind and SF1 carries no sector, so they stay in (their scaled accruals are mostly mid-distribution). Untested splits that the gate cannot report: filings that come separately after the release versus filed on the release day; long versus short side.","references":[{"cite":"Sloan (1996) Do stock prices fully reflect information in accruals and cash flows about future earnings? The Accounting Review","year":1996},{"cite":"Balsam, Bartov, Marquardt (2002) Accruals management, investor sophistication, and equity valuation: evidence from 10-Q filings. Journal of Accounting Research 40(4)","year":2002},{"cite":"Livnat, Santicchia (2006) Cash flows, accruals, and future returns. Financial Analysts Journal 62(4)","year":2006}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: sharadar_sep (ret_co, ret_oc, dollar_volume, tradable, extras liq_rank) and the as-reported quarterly SF1 fields sf1_arq_netinc, sf1_arq_ncfo, sf1_arq_assets (usable from the session after the SEC filing date, as the loader delivers them). Decisions after the close of each session t, trades at the open of t+1. (1) Filing event: stock j has a filing event on session t if j is a LIQ-500 member at t, the tuple (sf1_arq_netinc, sf1_arq_ncfo, sf1_arq_assets) at t differs from the tuple at t-1 in at least one field (NaN to a value counts as a change), all three values are non-NaN at t, sf1_arq_assets > 0, and j had no accepted filing event in the previous 40 sessions (drops amendments and re-filings of the same quarter). No events in the first 63 sessions of the data view (warm-up: values loaded on the first rows are not new filings). (2) Score: quarterly accruals acc = (sf1_arq_netinc - sf1_arq_ncfo) / sf1_arq_assets, all three from the same latest filing. (3) Breakpoints: on each session t, compute acc for every current LIQ-500 member with non-NaN values (the latest filing of each, whatever its date, as delivered by the loader); if fewer than 100 members have a value, no events that day. Let lo = the leg_quantile quantile and hi = the (1 - leg_quantile) quantile of that cross-section. (4) Side: a filing event with acc <= lo is a long event (+1), with acc >= hi a short event (-1); filers in between are not events. (5) Book: each event opens a position at the open of t+1 with a fixed weight of +0.04 (long event) or -0.04 (short event), held for hold_days sessions and closed at the open of session t+1+hold_days. No re-equalizing of weights between entry and exit. If a stock leaves LIQ-500 or is not tradable during the hold, its position is closed at the first decision row where that happens (the engine allows no weight outside the universe). A stock already held gets no second position; a new event on a held stock is ignored. If the new entries of a session would take the gross above 1.0, all of that session's new entries are scaled by the same factor so that gross equals 1.0. Cash otherwise. Long and short legs are not forced to balance (market_exposure long_short).","params":{"hold_days":{"grid":[3,5,8],"value":5},"leg_quantile":{"grid":[0.1,0.2,0.3],"value":0.2}},"timeframes":["1d","1q"]},"title":"Accrual information at the 10-Q/10-K filing - LIQ-500 long/short, long low-accrual and short high-accrual filers from the second session after the SEC filing, hold 5 days","universe":{"kind":"liq_n","n":500}}

title: Earnings-seasonality surprise - LIQ-500 market-neutral, long seasonally strong / short seasonally weak upcoming quarters, 5 sessions around the predicted 8-K release
