the signal needs up to 26 accepted quarters of history, so the view must start in 1998","fields":["sf1_arq_netinc"],"frequency":"1q","period":["1998-01-02","2020-12-31"]},{"dataset":"sec_8k_item202","description":"earnings-release reaction sessions; events need last year's same-quarter release, so the first events come about one year after the start","fields":["ea_reaction_day"],"frequency":"event","period":["2004-08-23","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return of the events is below the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the latest third of the dev event sample has the wrong sign (decay after publication or no effect in recent large caps); the card counts this as a refutation even if two thirds are right-signed.","Mechanism shape: if the 10-session abnormal return is more than twice the 5-session one, or the effect is already as large at the 1-session horizon as at 5 (before most releases fall in the window), the return is a slow style drift or stock-selection artefact, not a correction at the release, and the claim is wrong.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or the bootstrap lower bound of Sharpe minus T-bill Sharpe not above zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbours (years_back 4 and 6, threshold 0.70 and 0.80, and their combinations) beat the T-bill bar, or the book loses its edge at doubled costs."],"family":"anomalies-at-earnings-news","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Investors (and the consensus they follow) who extrapolate the latest quarterly earnings level: they sell or avoid firms coming off a seasonally weak quarter and bid up firms coming off a seasonally strong one, then are surprised at the next release. Liquidity traders who sell the high-seasonality name (or buy the low-seasonality name) into the release supply the other side.","why":"Many firms have a stable seasonal earnings pattern: the same fiscal quarter is strong (or weak) relative to the neighbouring quarters year after year. Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon and Soltes (2017) show that investors and analysts underweight this predictable pattern and anchor on the most recent quarters, so expectations for a seasonally strong quarter are too low and for a seasonally weak quarter too high. The error is revealed when the quarter's earnings are released: firms entering a positive-seasonality quarter earn higher returns at the release than firms entering a negative-seasonality quarter, and analyst forecast errors are more positive in positive-seasonality quarters, so the return is an expectation error corrected at the news, not a risk premium. The claim is concentrated at the release, so a short window around the release date is the natural test horizon.","why_not_arbitraged":"The edge per release is small next to the idiosyncratic jump risk of an earnings release, so a book that harvests it carries large single-name event risk for a thin mean; it needs firm-level quarterly histories over five years and the release calendar of every firm; its capacity is concentrated in a few weeks per quarter; and the bias sits in analysts' and investors' expectation formation, which the paper shows had not disappeared over decades."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of session t, a LIQ-500 stock whose same-quarter earnings release of last year was 248 sessions ago (first Item 2.02 reaction session in a 40-session cluster), with no release in the last 40 sessions, has an earnings-seasonality score S for its upcoming quarter (mean over the last 5 years of the rank of that fiscal quarter's net income among its four neighbouring quarters) of at least 0.75 (side +1, expected to outperform the other members through the release window) or at most 0.25 (side -1, expected to underperform).","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks, LIQ-500 cross-section, 5-session hold, mechanism test declared, and it combines a quarterly fundamental signal (1q) with a daily event clock (1d). Why this is not a retry. H-0053 (return seasonality, monthly, dead) named this test as its open question: 'the earnings-month component could be tested with real release dates'. H-0023 (date-only announcement premium) marked long only, so the premium itself drove its placebo comparison; here both sides are marked at the same release clock, so any generic announcement premium cancels and the placebo mean should be near zero. H-0032 (accruals/profitability/asset-growth composite around the predicted release) used slow style anomalies whose return is not specific to one release; earnings seasonality is a claim about the earnings of exactly the quarter being released, with a documented analyst forecast error, so it should show up in the window and not build for weeks (falsification criterion 3 checks this). Family: filed under anomalies-at-earnings-news because the mechanism is the same (a predictable expectation error corrected at earnings news), and the predicted-date clock is shared with H-0023, H-0026 and H-0032, so the trials should count together. Design choices argued in advance, not tuned: the five-quarter centred rank instead of the paper's rank over 20 quarters, because the paper's measure puts the same-quarter observations at the oldest end of each year and so tilts the long leg toward shrinking firms (a growth confound); net income instead of EPS so splits do not break the history; threshold 0.75 = 'beat three of four neighbours on average'; 248 sessions = one session before a 5-session window centred on last year's date plus 52 weeks (about 251 sessions). Forecasts (K-0098, K-0120, K-0125): about 350-400 LIQ-500 members with 5.5 years of consistent quarters and 8-K coverage, four anchors a year each, 20-30 % beyond the thresholds: roughly 2500-7000 events on 1200-2000 dates from late 2005 to 2020 (state a shortfall below 2000 as a sign that the quarter-sequence rule drops too many stocks). Round trip from the cost tiers: 6 bps (rank up to 200) to 12 bps (rank 200-500), about 10 bps on average. Expected gross per event 10-30 bps (the paper's long-short alpha is about 62 bps a month in announcement months, value-weighted about the same, so large firms carry it); the both-sides design should put the placebo bar near or under cost, so a tradable effect can pass. Book: about 7 open events on an average day, 20 or more in peak earnings weeks, slot weight 0.05, so mean exposure about 0.3-0.45 including the hedge, clustered in earnings seasons. Expected annual gain: with 15 bps net per event and about 375 events a year at 0.05, roughly 2-3 % a year at an annual volatility of about 5 % (release-day jumps dominate), so a net Sharpe of about 0.4-0.6; the book clears the 0.5 floor only if gross per event is about 30 bps or more. Most likely deaths, in order: the latest third is weak or wrong-signed (published 2014 on SSRN, 2017 in print; dev holds about four post-print years), the predicted window misses many releases (dilution: the hit rate of 'last year plus 52 weeks' in large caps is unmeasured, K-0035), the book misses the absolute Sharpe floor although the event study passes (K-0064). Data caveats for the Builder: if Sharadar ARQ lacks fourth-quarter rows, the 120-session gap rule voids most scores; fail loudly (report the share of scored LIQ-500 members by year) rather than silently trading a handful of stocks. The beta gap between legs should be small (both legs mix sectors, which rotate with the season), but retailers dominate one leg in the fourth-quarter season; a by-side and by-season report would be welcome if the gate can give one.","references":[{"cite":"Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon, Soltes (2017) Being Surprised by the Unsurprising: Earnings Seasonality and Stock Returns, Review of Financial Studies 30(1)","year":2017}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs (all point-in-time): LIQ-500 membership and liq_rank, total returns, the SEC 8-K Item 2.02 flag ea_reaction_day (1 on the reaction session of an earnings release), and the as-reported quarterly net income sf1_arq_netinc (usable from the day after the filing). (1) Quarter history per stock: walk the daily sf1_arq_netinc series of each stock up to the decision day t. A change of value starts a new fiscal quarter if at least 40 sessions have passed since the last accepted quarter started; a change within 40 sessions overwrites the value of the latest accepted quarter (amendment). Record each accepted quarter's value and the session it became usable. If two consecutive accepted quarters are more than 120 sessions apart anywhere in the span used below, the stock has no score (a missing quarter would misalign the seasons). Lag 1 = the latest accepted quarter, lag 2 the one before, and so on; the upcoming quarter (the one to be released next) is lag 0. (2) Seasonality score S for the upcoming quarter, with Y = years_back: for each k = 1..Y, the same fiscal quarter k years earlier is lag 4k; compare its net income with its four neighbouring quarters at lags 4k-2, 4k-1, 4k+1, 4k+2 and set r_k = (number of neighbours it exceeds + 0.5 x number of ties) / 4, in [0, 1]. S = mean of r_1..r_Y. This needs lags up to 4Y+2 and is neutral to a linear earnings trend (the same-quarter observation sits in the middle of its five-quarter block). S = 1 means the upcoming quarter was the best of its neighbourhood every year; S = 0 the worst. (3) Alignment guard: let R1 be the most recent reaction session of the stock in the sessions t-120 .. t-40. The stock is scored only if R1 exists and the latest accepted quarter became usable no earlier than 5 sessions before R1 (so lag 1 is the quarter released at R1, not the one before it). (4) Event (decision after the close of session t): stock j is a member of LIQ-500 on t; session t-248 was a reaction session of j (ea_reaction_day = 1) and it was the first reaction session of j within the 40 sessions up to and including t-248 (extra Item 2.02 filings in a cluster do not anchor); j had no reaction session in t-39 .. t (the upcoming release has not come early); j is not already in an open event; S exists. Last year's same-quarter release was 248 sessions ago, so this year's release is expected about 251 sessions after it, i.e. around session t+3, and the holding window t+1 .. t+5 is centred on it. Side +1 (long) if S >= threshold, side -1 (short) if S <= 1 - threshold, no event otherwise. (5) Book: market-neutral. Each event opens at the open of t+1 with weight +0.05 (long) or -0.05 (short) and is closed at the open of t+6 (decision after the close of t+5), i.e. held 5 sessions; an event whose stock leaves LIQ-500 is closed at the next decision instead. Every day the net dollar exposure of the open events is hedged with equal weights across the 100 most liquid LIQ-500 members (lowest liq_rank) that are not in an open event, so the book is dollar-neutral. If gross exposure exceeds 1.0, all weights (events and hedge) are scaled down proportionally. Days without open events are in cash. Missing returns or a stock without the required history simply yield no event; no fills for non-tradable stocks.","params":{"threshold":{"grid":[0.7,0.75,0.8],"value":0.75},"years_back":{"grid":[4,5,6],"value":5}},"timeframes":["1d","1q"]},"title":"Earnings-seasonality surprise - LIQ-500 market-neutral, long seasonally strong / short seasonally weak upcoming quarters, 5 sessions around the predicted 8-K release","universe":{"kind":"liq_n","n":500}}

title: News-conditioned drift vs reversal, learned - LIQ-500 dollar-neutral, LightGBM on own-move, earnings-release, volume and volatility features, daily 5-day cohorts
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","frequency":"1d","period":["2004-09-01","2026-09-25"]},{"dataset":"sec_8k_item202","fields":["ea_reaction_day"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2004-09-01","2026-09-25"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: entries to the top and bottom score legs (side +1 / -1) do not beat the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos at 5 sessions, or their gross side-adjusted abnormal return per event is below the round-trip cost (cost ratio < 1): the combination did not lift the sub-cost effects above cost, which extends K-0079 to a nonlinear composite.","Mechanism: the latest third of dev (about 2015-2020) has the wrong sign (K-0060 kill condition).","Mechanism shape: the 1-session horizon carries no part of the 5-session effect (the attention and drift components are front-loaded; a pure slow build means the score found a style, not the events).","Net Sharpe on dev below 0.5 against T-bills, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference below zero.","Neighbors of n_estimators 100 or leg_fraction 0.1 fail G2 (fewer than 75 % beat the benchmark, or median neighbor Sharpe below 0.7 x primary).","Net Sharpe at doubled costs below the T-bill benchmark (the book turns over about fully every five sessions).","A ridge regression (framework ridge) on the same six features with the same label, refit schedule and book gives a net Sharpe within 0.10 of the gbm or better: the nonlinearity is not what pays."],"family":"short-term-reversal","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"On no-news days, impatient traders who demand liquidity with market orders and pay the concession to whoever takes the other side; after extreme moves, attention-driven buyers at the next open; after earnings releases, investors who underreact to the news and sell (buy) too early into good (bad) news.","why":"The sign of what follows a large stock-specific move depends on why it moved. Moves on an earnings-release session carry information that investors underreact to, so they drift in the same direction for days (the lab reproduced this on real 8-K dates: H-0028, H-0031, H-0033). Moves without an earnings release are on average order-flow pressure, so they partly reverse as liquidity providers who absorbed the imbalance are paid (H-0030 cleared the placebo bar). Extreme moves of either sign also draw attention buying at the next open that gives back over the next sessions (H-0069 cleared the placebo bar in all thirds). Each of these effects is real in LIQ-500 but alone sits at or below the round-trip cost. They are partly independent and act on the same variable (the recent move) with opposite signs depending on the news state, so a single score that conditions the slope of the move on the release flag, on abnormal volume and on volatility should be larger at its extremes than any one-variable sort. The card tests whether that combination lifts the per-event gross above cost.","why_not_arbitraged":"Each piece is small relative to the spread of a taker, so a single-signal book does not pay (K-0079); bearing the inventory risk of a high-volatility stock for a week is capital-intensive and rationed exactly when the concession is largest; telling news from no-news moves at scale needs filing-time data that many short-horizon traders do not condition on."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of t the stock is in the top leg_fraction (side +1) or the bottom leg_fraction (side -1) of the walk-forward model score among scored LIQ-500 members, i.e. it enters that day's long or short cohort.","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["z1: day-t residual return (stock minus LIQ-500 equal-weight mean) divided by 63-day volatility; the size and sign of today's stock-specific move, the variable whose next-week slope the mechanism says flips with the news state","z5: residual return over t-4..t scaled by 63-day volatility times sqrt(5); slower order-flow pressure that liquidity providers are still unwinding over the week","ea5: 1 if an 8-K Item 2.02 earnings-release reaction session (sec_8k_item202 ea_reaction_day) fell in t-4..t; the news state that separates information-driven moves (drift) from no-news pressure (reversal)","ea_z: volatility-scaled residual return on the most recent release session in t-4..t, 0 if none; the market's own measure of the earnings surprise (the reaction-drift input of H-0028)","dv_ab: log of 5-day mean dollar volume over the prior 63-session mean; attention and order-imbalance intensity (an extreme move on heavy volume without news is the attention give-back case)","lvol: log 63-day realized volatility of daily total returns; inventory risk of the liquidity provider, which scales the concession demanded for absorbing flow"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"The mechanism is a sign flip and a V shape, which a ridge on the same six features cannot represent. (a) The slope of next-week return on the recent move z1/z5 is negative (reversal) when ea5 = 0 and positive (drift) when a release was in the window: a linear model fits one average slope that partly cancels the two. (b) The attention give-back hits both tails (extreme up and extreme down moves underperform next), a function of |z1| that is invisible to a linear term in signed z1; combined with reversal, large up-moves should be the clearest shorts and large down-moves weaker longs, an asymmetry. (c) The concession should grow with volatility and with abnormal volume only for no-news moves (a three-way interaction). Depth-3 trees (8 leaves) can express each of these; who pays is the same as in the mechanism (liquidity demanders on no-news days, attention buyers, earnings underreactors). If ridge on the same features with the same schedule and book is as good, the claim is false and the card measured plain reversal."},"notes":"Why this is not a re-run of dead cards: H-0030 (no-news reversal), H-0069 (attention give-back) and H-0028/H-0031 (earnings-reaction drift) each tested one effect with a hand-written sort; the first two cleared the placebo bar but stayed under cost, the drift books lost to T-bills. K-0079 says conditioners changed significance, not size relative to cost. This card asks the one question those cards could not: whether a learned score that lets the slope of the move depend on the news state, volume and volatility is large enough at its extremes to clear cost. It is the lab's first learned-model card and names its linear baseline. Family: filed under short-term-reversal because most non-release-season scores will be reversal of no-news moves; the earnings-drift part shares events with post-earnings-announcement-drift, so the Chair may prefer to count it there too. Forecasts (written before any result): scored members about 450-500 per day from late 2006 (the expanding window needs about two years of labels before the first fit; the exact start is the framework's), legs of about 45-50 names each, so roughly 90-100 events per date on about 3,300-3,500 dates in dev, i.e. 300,000-350,000 events. Round trip 6-12 bps (half-spread 3 bps to rank 200, 6 bps to rank 500; the legs lean to ranks 200-500, so take about 10 bps). Expected gross side-adjusted abnormal return per event at 5 sessions: 8-20 bps (central 12), i.e. near cost; the placebo bar for a dense daily set should lie well below cost, so a failure will be a cost verdict, not a power one. Book arithmetic: with 12 bps per 5 sessions per side the dollar-neutral gross-1 book earns about 6 %/yr gross; full turnover every five sessions at about 10 bps round trip costs about 4-5 %/yr, minus less for names that persist in a leg; net excess about 1-3 %/yr at 4-6 % volatility, Sharpe 0.2-0.6 against the 0.5 bar. So the most likely death is G1 on the absolute Sharpe floor or G2 on doubled costs, even if the mechanism passes. Mean exposure about 0.85 (flat until the first fit). Beta: the long leg will lean toward high-volatility recent losers, so the dollar-neutral book likely carries a small positive beta (K-0074); the event study compares raw returns with unmarked peers, so a beta gap between legs partly cancels because both sides are marked. It is larger when the reaction shows real news, not opening noise: the opening gap is confirmed by the regular-session move of the same day (institutions trading with the news during the day, not fading a retail-driven open), it comes on heavy release-session volume, it was not anticipated by a pre-release run-up in the same direction, and it has the same sign as the stock's previous release reaction (serially correlated earnings news, which investors treat as independent each quarter; Bernard and Thomas). (1) Confirmation: drift should follow when gap and intraday move have the same sign and be weak or reversed when the session fades the gap. That is a product of signs, while ridge only adds gap and intraday linearly, so a large faded gap and a large confirmed gap get similar scores. (2) Anticipation: a run-up in the same direction as the reaction should cut the drift and an opposite run-up should raise it, again an interaction of the run-up with the reaction sign. (3) Persistence: a reaction with the same sign as the previous release should drift more (Bernard and Thomas), an interaction of prev_reaction_z with the current sign. (4) Threshold: small reactions are noise, so the payoff is flat near zero and rises only beyond a size, and abnormal volume should amplify only large reactions. How it differs from earlier cards: (a) from H-0033 (positive-reaction tilt on a cap-weighted core, just under the margin), it selects events by a learned score trained only on release events, with features about the reaction's quality (gap versus regular session, volume, anticipation, persistence) rather than a reaction-size cut. Slot weight 0.02, cap 0.30 and hold 5 were set before seeing anything, from the K-0046 finding that the drift sits in the first sessions. They were not tuned to H-0033's miss (whose exact values I cannot see). (b) From H-0094 (learned score over all rows, own-move, release, volume and volatility features, dollar-neutral daily cohorts, died on cost): this model never sees non-release rows, so it does not mix no-news reversal and attention give-back into the score, and it has no short side, no hedge basket and no flat-otherwise book (K-0027, K-0031). FORECASTS (K-0098, K-0120, K-0125): release events among LIQ-500 members with 8-K coverage about 1,400-1,800 a year from 2005; first fit about two years later, so scored events about 2007-2020, about 20,000-24,000; tilt entries (top 30 %) about 6,000-7,000 on about 2,000-2,500 dates (G1 events), about 450-500 a year. Gross exposure is always 1.0. Round trip per slot: 6-12 bps for the event stock (3/6 bps half spread by rank) plus about 6 bps for the core funding trades, about 12-18 bps. Needed: about 40 bps gross abnormal return per entry over 5 sessions for about +2 %/year over the core, which is roughly +0.10-0.15 Sharpe at about 17 % book volatility. If the selected events earn only what a plain reaction-size cut earns (K-0130: treat forecasts as upper bounds), the book falls just short of the margin as H-0033 did, and the ridge criterion will show whether selection added anything. Confounds: the cap-weighted core built from filed market caps is a proxy for SPY (staleness up to a quarter, LIQ-500 rather than S&P 500 membership), so part of the difference to SPY can be the core. Tilt-entry stocks may have a higher beta than their peers (K-0074), which inflates the raw abnormal return in up markets. Training sample: a few thousand event rows at the first fit and tens of thousands by 2020, with 6 features and 8-leaf trees with min_child_samples 200, so the model capacity is small on purpose. 8-K coverage leans toward survivors (K-0035). Entry at the open of t+1, exit at the open of t+6 (5 sessions); a stock that leaves the universe during the hold is closed at the first decision where it is no longer a member; a second event of the same stock inside its hold does not add a slot. Tilt = 0.02 per open slot, added on top of the slot stock's core weight; if the open slots would exceed a total tilt of 0.30, all new slots of that date are scaled down equally so the total is 0.30 (existing slots keep their weight). seasonal random-walk earnings expectation and are surprised in a predictable direction at the release, and traders who demand immediacy in the sessions before a release (pre-positioning, hedging, de-risking) and pay the inventory concession to whoever takes the other side.","why":"Prices underweight the time-series properties of quarterly earnings: seasonal earnings changes are positively autocorrelated at a one-quarter lag and negatively at a four-quarter lag, and a large part of the resulting mispricing is corrected at the next earnings release, when the actual number replaces the naive seasonal expectation (Bernard and Thomas 1990). Separately, liquidity providers demand a larger concession for absorbing order flow just before a release, because their inventory then carries jump risk, so pre-release price moves reverse more than moves at other times (So and Wang 2014). Both claims say the same features have a different, stronger slope inside the few sessions around a release than on ordinary days, and that the payoff scales with how large the release jump of the firm usually is. The card tests exactly that conditional structure: one model is trained on all stock-days with a release-window flag as a feature, and only window entrants are traded.","why_not_arbitraged":"The trade is a short, jumpy bet on single-stock release sessions: idiosyncratic jump risk is large relative to the expected edge, it needs both legs (shorting announcers before a release is costly and risky), it is spread over thousands of small positions clustered in earnings seasons, and market makers' capital is the scarce resource the reversal part is paying for."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"A LIQ-500 member is a release-window entrant (t is the third session before its predicted 8-K earnings release, last year's reaction session + 364 days, no release in the last 20 sessions) and its gbm score percentile among all members on t puts it in the long leg (side +1, percentile >= 1 - leg_fraction) or the short leg (side -1, percentile <= leg_fraction), on a day when both legs are non-empty.","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["win: 0/1 flag, t is the third session before the stock's predicted release (last year's real 8-K Item 2.02 reaction session + 364 calendar days) and no release in the last 20 sessions; the lag-4 surprise with negative autocorrelation (sharadar_sf1)","ear1: the stock's return minus the universe mean return on its most recent ea_reaction_day session, divided by vol63 at that session; the typical size of the stock's release jump, which scales every payoff above (sharadar_sep)"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"train_days":1260,"why_not_linear":"A ridge on the same six features applies one slope per feature to every stock-day; the win flag can only shift the level of window rows, and that level is cancelled by the cross-sectional label ranking and the dollar-neutral book. The mechanism is a slope change: sue1, sue4 and ear1 should predict much more strongly inside the release window (the mispricing is corrected at the release) than on the ~98 % of ordinary rows, pre10 should reverse more strongly inside the window (inventory risk of liquidity providers before a jump), and all of it should grow with vol63 (a product, not a sum). Trees that split on win and vol63 first can express exactly these interactions with 8 leaves; a linear model cannot. Who pays: seasonal-random-walk anchored investors at the release and pre-release liquidity demanders. If ridge on the same features does as well, the window concentration claim is wrong."},"notes":"Why this is not a near copy. H-0093 (same family) used the same predicted-window rule with one sort on earnings seasonality and ended with gross about equal to cost; H-0064 (short-term-reversal) sorted on the 3-session pre-release return and passed the mechanism above cost but faded in the latest third; H-0094 combined reversal and news features on all days and stayed under cost. This card asks a different question that none of them could: whether earnings-information and liquidity features have a different slope INSIDE predicted release windows than on ordinary days, which is what both Bernard-Thomas and So-Wang imply and what a single sort cannot show. The pre10 feature overlaps H-0064's mechanism; the Chair may count this card against short-term-reversal too. The family is anomalies-at-earnings-news because the core claim (known earnings information is priced at the next release) is that family's mechanism. Linear baseline: ridge on the same six features with the same schedule and book; the card names it as a falsification criterion and asks the Skeptic or Librarian to have it run. Useful descriptive control if the framework allows: the same gbm score traded on non-window rows at the same count per date (should earn clearly less). Arithmetic written in advance (K-0053, K-0098, K-0120, K-0130). Events: LIQ-500 members with a real release one year earlier, about 1500-1800 window entrants a year from 2005-08 on (8-K data start 2004-08 plus one year), about half to two thirds placed in a leg at leg_fraction 0.33 and on days with both sides present: roughly 800-1100 events a year, 12000-16000 in dev on about 2000-2600 dates (clustered in earnings seasons, few in the quiet weeks). Round trip from the cost tiers: 6 bps per side for ranks 200-500, 5 bps floor, so about 10-12 bps. The 5-session window return of an announcer has a standard deviation of roughly 6-8 %; a score with a rank IC of 0.03-0.05 among window entrants gives a side-adjusted gross of about 20-35 bps per event, 2-3 times cost; literature spreads are an upper bound and the realistic case is the low end. If gross is only about 15 bps the book cannot reach the 0.5 Sharpe floor: that is the most likely death. Exposure: cohort gross min(0.20, 0.02 x marked) with 5 overlapping cohorts; peak-season days hit the cap, quiet weeks are flat, so mean gross exposure is expected around 0.25-0.40 (forecast from the busiest and quietest weeks, K-0125), above the 0.20 floor. Expected net Sharpe if gross is 25 bps: about 0.8-1.0; at 15 bps: about 0.3. Hit rate of the predicted date is unknown (K-0035, K-0036): large caps keep stable release calendars, so the 364-day rule with a window covering P-1 to P+2 is expected to contain the real release for most entrants, but early 2005-2006 coverage gaps and firms that changed their calendar dilute it. A release that happens before the entry is removed by the 20-session rule. SF1 net income is as reported (ARQ) and stale values after 400 days are NaN. Runtime: rolling 1260-row window on about 500 members is about 600k training rows, about 70 refits from 2003 on, 100 trees of at most 16 leaves: a few minutes per run on the lab machine. RAM: three attached fields. The 1q timeframe refers to the quarterly fundamentals and the yearly release anchor; decisions are daily.","references":[{"cite":"Bernard, V. L. and Thomas, J. K. (2014) News-driven return reversals: Liquidity provision ahead of earnings announcements, Journal of Financial Economics","year":2014}],"signal":{"description":"Data up to the close of day t, decision after the close of t, trades at the open of t+1. PREDICTED RELEASE: for each stock, every past session r with ea_reaction_day = 1 predicts a release session P = the first XNYS session on or after r + 364 calendar days (same weekday one year later). WINDOW ENTRY FLAG win[t, j] = 1 if (a) session t is exactly 3 sessions before a predicted P of stock j (so the 5-session hold from the open of t+1 to the open of t+6 spans the reaction sessions P-1 .. P+2), and (b) stock j had no ea_reaction_day = 1 in the 20 sessions up to and including t (otherwise it already reported this quarter); win = 0 on every other row, and 0 where ea_reaction_day is NaN. FEATURES (six, per stock and date, all from data known at the close of t; the five continuous ones are cross-sectionally rank-normalized and z-scored across the members of date t with the framework helper; win is passed as 0/1 unscaled): win; sue1; sue4; ear1; pre10; vol63 (definitions in ml.features). A stock with any missing continuous feature is not scored on that date. LABEL: total return from the open of t+1 to the open of t+6 (horizon 5), ranked across the universe on each date (framework label). MODEL: lab.framework.ml.walk_forward with model gbm (LightGBM), trained on ALL member rows (window and non-window), rolling training window of 1260 rows, refit every 63 rows, framework purge and seeds. Fixed settings: n_estimators 100, learning_rate 0.05, min_child_samples 200; num_leaves is the grid parameter. BOOK (score_weights + only_on): each day t, candidates = members with win = 1 and a score. For each candidate take the percentile of its score among the scores of all members on t. Long the candidates with percentile >= 1 - leg_fraction, short those with percentile <= leg_fraction. A cohort is opened only if it has at least one long and one short; its gross is g = min(0.20, 0.02 x number of marked names), +g/2 split equally across the longs and -g/2 equally across the shorts (dollar-neutral per cohort). investors who avoid holding systematic risk into scheduled releases; and, outside the windows, leverage-constrained investors who bid up high-beta stocks.","why":"Scheduled, pre-announced dates change what systematic risk earns over the following days, and the change is delivered through market beta, not through stock picking. (1) Month turn: institutions that need cash for month-end payments sell liquid equities in the last sessions of the month and reinvest payroll, pension and coupon inflows in the first sessions of the next (Ogden 1990; Etula, Rinne, Suominen and Vaittinen 2020), so the market return is concentrated around the turn and high-beta stocks collect most of it. (2) Scheduled macro releases (CPI, jobs report, FOMC statement): the beta-return relation is steeply positive on announcement days and flat or negative on other days (Savor and Wilson 2014). (3) On ordinary days leverage-constrained investors overpay for high-beta stocks, so a low-risk tilt is the better static holding. Taken together the best stock characteristic to hold for the next five sessions flips with the calendar position of the decision date. The lab has already seen part (1) clear the mechanism test twice in LIQ-500 (H-0016, H-0025) without a tradable book; this card asks whether a learned overlay that combines the calendar clocks with beta, volatility and liquidity, and holds a low-risk tilt outside the windows, turns that into an always-invested book that beats SPY.","why_not_arbitraged":"The reward is a systematic-risk premium paid on a few sessions per month, not a riskless spread: harvesting it means rotating an equity book into high beta a few times a month, which costs spread on every switch and carries full market risk in the window. The claim is that the sign of the beta and volatility tilt flips with the calendar position (high beta for windows that contain the month turn or a scheduled release, low risk otherwise), which only an interaction between a date feature and a stock feature can express; trees split on the calendar clock and then on beta. So the ridge baseline is the exact null 'calendar adds nothing', and the time-shifted placebo of G1 (same stocks, other dates) removes the static tilt as well. Who pays: month-end liquidity demanders and release-risk avoiders inside the windows, leverage-constrained beta buyers outside."},"notes":"BRIEF FIT. Short horizon (5-session label = holding), US single stocks cross-sectional (LIQ-500), learned model (gbm) with a ridge baseline named. I did not find a fresh price/volume, earnings, filing or ownership feature set for a 1-5 day learned card that the lab has not already used (H-0094 own-move/volume/vol, H-0095/H-0096 earnings releases, H-0097 filings, study 11 fundamentals/insiders/13F); date-level features are the one structural gap in the lab's ML cards, and the only date-level effects with a mechanism pass in LIQ-500 are calendar flows. (a) It answers the open question H-0025 left: 'is it the month-turn flow or low beta plus an equal-weight tilt? Only a same-universe control separates them.' Here two controls do exactly that: the time-shifted placebo (same stocks, other dates) at G1 and the ridge baseline, which cannot use the calendar at all. (b) The window, the characteristic (beta vs volatility vs liquidity) and the static tilt outside the window are learned walk-forward, not chosen by me after seeing H-0016/H-0025, and the scheduled macro releases are added inside equities, the route K-0063 left open ('a beta sort inside equities on announcement days removes the equity-versus-bond drift'). (c) It is the always-invested overlay that the H-0016 and K-0027 lessons asked for. Nothing in it retunes post_days, beta_lookback or leg_quantile of H-0025. The release-day feature shares its mechanism with the former macro-announcement-premium cards (now merged into variance-risk-premium-timing); if the Chair prefers, count this trial there as well. I did not open a new family name. FORECASTS (K-0098, K-0120, K-0130). Events = entries into the top fifth: about 10 per day on ordinary days and 50-80 on the 2-4 dates a month when the calendar tilt switches, so roughly 15-25 per session, 70,000- 120,000 events on 4,500-5,000 dates (first fit about two to three years into dev, cash before). title: Overnight gap vs intraday follow-through in earnings releases, learned - LIQ-500 long-only core plus 5-day tilt into top LightGBM-scored 8-K releases; mechanism test = gbm-only vs ridge-only picks
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","dollar_volume"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2004-01-02","2020-12-31"]},{"dataset":"sec_8k_item202","fields":["ea_reaction_day"],"frequency":"event","period":["2004-08-23","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism (central claim): the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return of gbm-only top picks (+1) versus ridge-only top picks (-1) on release rows does not exceed the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or its gross per event is below the round-trip cost: the nonlinear model adds nothing over a linear one on the same split features.","The latest third of the dev event sample has the wrong sign (K-0060), even if the pooled test passes.","The disagreement return is wrong-signed at the 1-session horizon and appears only at 10 sessions or later: slow drift, not release information.","Ridge (framework ridge, alpha 1.0) on the same features, rows, schedule and book gives the same or a higher net Sharpe than the gbm book.","Net Sharpe on dev below SPY_TR + 0.10, or the stationary-bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference below zero.","Fewer than 75 % of the neighbours of n_estimators 100 and top_q 0.2 beat SPY_TR, or the book does not beat SPY_TR at doubled costs."],"family":"post-earnings-announcement-drift","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Investors who trade the release session against the overnight news (intraday faders who treat the gap as an opening-auction overreaction when it was information) and investors anchored on the pre-release price who under-react; when the gap is an attention imbalance, the retail and attention buyers at the open pay.","why":"The market's reaction to an earnings release has two parts with different traders behind them. The overnight gap (previous close to the open of the reaction session) is set in thin after-hours and pre-open trading and in the opening auction, where attention-driven and retail orders are concentrated (Berkman et al. 2012 show that attention-grabbing stocks open high and give it back intraday). The intraday part (open to close of the reaction session) is traded by institutions that have the full release and usually the conference call. Recent work on overnight/intraday decomposition around releases reports that the overnight reaction carries the information about later returns while intraday trading often runs against it (a tug of war between clienteles, Lou, Polk and Skouras 2019). Drift after the release (Bernard and Thomas 1989) should therefore depend on how the reaction was split, not only on its total size, and the dependence is not additive: a gap carries information only when it is large relative to the stock's own volatility (a news gap, not an opening-auction imbalance), its predictive sign can flip with the size of the intraday fade (a full reversal of the gap by institutions versus a partial clientele fade), and heavy release-session volume and a pre-release run-up in the same direction change how much is still unpriced. A tree model on the split can represent these thresholds and sign changes; a linear model with one slope per feature cannot.","why_not_arbitraged":"The edge per release is a few tens of basis points in single names with high idiosyncratic risk on the release week, spread over hundreds of small positions a year; capacity is limited by the spread on the reaction day, and the split-dependent part is a small conditional refinement of a well-known but slowly decaying drift that most quantitative funds take only through the total surprise."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"On a release row (8-K Item 2.02 reaction session, LIQ-500 member), exactly one of two walk-forward models fitted on the same six features, rows and schedule puts the stock in its top_q of trailing-252-session release scores: side +1 when only the gbm does (a nonlinear pick), side -1 when only the ridge does (a linear pick).","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["gap_z: reaction-session overnight return ret_co[t] over the stock's 63-day daily volatility (the after-hours / opening-auction part of the reaction, set by attention-driven and pre-open traders)","session_z: reaction-session open-to-close return ret_oc[t] over 63-day volatility (the part traded by institutions with the full release and call)","vol_shock: log of reaction-session dollar volume over its 63-day median (intensity of disagreement and attention on the release)","runup_z: 21-session total return before the reaction session over 63-day volatility scaled to 21 days (how much of the news was anticipated)","log sigma63: 63-day daily volatility (uncertainty and limits to arbitrage)","log of the 63-day median dollar volume (size, analyst coverage and liquidity proxy; slower diffusion in less covered names)"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"The claim is that the drift is not an additive function of the two parts of the reaction. (a) Threshold: a gap smaller than about one own-volatility unit is an opening-auction imbalance that tends to revert, a larger gap is news that drifts, so the slope on gap_z changes sign with its size. (b) Sign interaction: a gap that institutions fully reverse during the session (session_z large and opposite) marks an opening overreaction, while a partial fade is clientele noise and the gap still drifts; the effect of session_z depends on the sign and size of gap_z. (c) Volume and anticipation gate both: heavy release-session volume and a run-up in the same direction leave less unpriced. A ridge on the same six z-scored features fits one slope per feature and can only express 'gap matters more than session'; it cannot express sign flips, thresholds or the gap x fade interaction. Who pays: intraday faders who trade against an informative gap, and attention buyers at the open when the gap was an imbalance. If ridge picks the same releases as the gbm, or its picks do as well, the nonlinearity claim is false; the mechanism test measures exactly that."},"notes":"Relation to earlier cards. Same family as H-0024, H-0028, H-0031, H-0033, H-0034 and H-0095, filed here on purpose so the trials count together. What is new: (1) the reaction is split into the overnight gap and the intraday session part, an information source none of those cards used (K-0136 asks for a new source, not a new learner); (2) the mechanism test is not 'top-scored releases drift' (H-0028/H-0033 already showed plain reaction drift passes) but the disagreement between a gbm and a ridge fitted on identical features, rows and schedule, which is the control K-0135 says has never run. diagnostic.py: run walk_forward twice (gbm with the card params, ridge alpha 1.0), compute each model's trailing-252-session percentile on every release row as in the entry rule; mask = rows where exactly one model is in its top_q; side = +1 where only the gbm is, -1 where only the ridge is. Forecast: about 13 000 scored release rows in LIQ-500 2006-2020 (H-0096 counted 15 600 events on the same flag), top fifth about 2 600 per model, overlap of the two top fifths about half, so about 1 100-1 400 events per side on roughly 1 500 dates; with a 5-day single-stock idiosyncratic sd near 4.5 % the placebo bar should sit near 20 bps, above a round trip of about 9-12 bps (rank tiers 3/6 bps half spread). So a pass needs a gbm-minus-ridge spread of over about 20 bps per event: a large nonlinearity premium, low prior. A failure with a bar above cost is a 'cannot tell' only if the average is clearly positive; an average near zero or negative closes the learned-model route on release events. Strategy arithmetic (K-0064, K-0098): about 195 entries a year x 5 sessions x 0.05 gives a mean sleeve near 0.19 (less in peak weeks where the 0.50 cap binds, K-0125); at 40-60 bps excess per entry the sleeve adds about 0.4-0.6 % a year, well under the roughly 1.5 % that a Sharpe margin of 0.10 over SPY needs. The book is therefore expected to fail the G1 margin unless top picks earn far more than the plain positive reactions of H-0033; the informative verdict is the mechanism test. Timing caveats: the reaction session is the first session whose close is at or after the 8-K acceptance; for releases inside market hours the gap holds no news (the model sees a small gap_z); when the 8-K is accepted a session after the press release the flagged session is one day late and its gap is not the reaction (dilution, not look-ahead). Pre-2004-08 rows have no events; the first fit needs a training sample, so events start about 2006. References: only Bernard and Thomas is listed formally; Berkman, Koch, Tuttle and Zhang (2012, JFQA, overnight returns and the cost of buying at the open) and Lou, Polk and Skouras (2019, JFE, tug of war between overnight and intraday returns) motivate the split but are not listed, to keep the publication-decay check on the drift itself. No new dataset is needed.","references":[{"cite":"Bernard, Thomas (1989) Post-earnings-announcement drift: delayed price response or risk premium? Journal of Accounting Research","year":1989}],"signal":{"description":"Data: sharadar_sep daily (ret_co = previous close to open, ret_oc = open to close, dollar_volume, universe membership) and the attached sec_8k_item202 flag ea_reaction_day. A release row is (t, j) with ea_reaction_day[t, j] == 1 and j a point-in-time LIQ-500 member on t. All features are computed after the close of t from data up to that close, for all columns (not only members, never with an ever-member list, see K-0134), and z-scored across the members of date t by the framework helper. Features: (1) gap_z = ret_co[t] / sigma63, sigma63 = standard deviation of daily close-to-close total returns over t-63..t-1; (2) session_z = ret_oc[t] / sigma63; (3) vol_shock = log(dollar_volume[t] / median dollar_volume over t-63..t-1); (4) runup_z = total return over t-21..t-1 / (sigma63 * sqrt(21)); (5) log sigma63; (6) log of the median dollar volume over t-63..t-1 (size and coverage proxy). Label: total return from the open of t+1 to the open of t+6 (horizon_days 5), ranked across the universe on each date by the framework. Model: lab.framework.ml.walk_forward with model gbm, trained only on release rows (sample mask = release rows; scores are produced only for release rows), expanding window, refit every 63 rows, fixed hyperparameters num_leaves 15, learning_rate 0.05, min_child_samples 200, subsample 0.8, colsample 1.0, and n_estimators from params. Before the first fit there are no scores. Entry rule: a release row (t, j) is a tilt entry when its gbm score is at or above the (1 - top_q) quantile of the gbm scores of all release rows in the trailing 252 sessions up to and including t (at least 100 scored rows in that window, otherwise no entries). Book (long-only, decided after the close of t, traded at the open of t+1): core = all LIQ-500 members of date t weighted by their 63-day median dollar volume (a capitalisation proxy), weights refreshed on the first session of each month and held as fixed fractions in between; sleeve = one slot of 0.05 for every active tilt entry, opened at the open of t+1 and closed at the open of t+6 (5 sessions), or earlier at the first decision row where the stock is no longer a member (engine rule, K-0051). Sleeve gross S_t = 0.05 x active slots, capped at 0.50 (all slots scaled proportionally when the cap binds). Final weights = (1 - S_t) x core + sleeve; a tilt stock also keeps its core weight. Total gross 1.0, no shorts. Stocks with a missing feature are not scored; a missing return or delisting follows the engine's terminal-return policy.","params":{"n_estimators":{"grid":[50,100,200],"value":100},"top_q":{"grid":[0.1,0.2,0.3],"value":0.2}},"timeframes":["1d"]},"title":"Overnight gap vs intraday follow-through in earnings releases, learned - LIQ-500 long-only core plus 5-day tilt into top LightGBM-scored 8-K releases; mechanism test = gbm-only vs ridge-only picks","universe":{"kind":"liq_n","n":500}}

title: Distraction-conditioned earnings-reaction drift, learned - LIQ-500 long-only 5-day slots in 8-K reactions ranked by LightGBM on reaction x market-wide release load
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","dollar_volume","tradable"],"frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"sec_8k_item202","fields":["ea_reaction_day"],"frequency":"event"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the 5-session abnormal return of entries (top-scored release rows, side +1) is not above the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per entry is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the latest third of dev has a negative mean abnormal return for entries (decay, K-0060), even if the pooled test passes.","Net Sharpe on dev below SPY_TR Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference at or below zero.","Fewer than 75 % of the grid neighbours of n_estimators 100 and top 0.3 beat the benchmark, or doubled costs leave the Sharpe below SPY_TR.","Ridge (framework ridge) on the same six features, rows, label and refit schedule gives entries with the same or higher 5-session gross: the nonlinearity (the attention interaction) is not what pays.","Entries on high-load sessions (load rank >= 0.5) or end-of-week sessions do not earn more than entries on the other sessions: the attention channel is absent and only plain reaction drift is left."],"family":"post-earnings-announcement-drift","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Investors whose attention is used up by competing releases (and by the weekend) and who trade on the news days later at prices that have only partly adjusted; the strategy buys from those still selling the stale price after good news.","why":"Investors have limited attention. Learned selections of which reactions drift (H-0095, H-0100) used only the stock's own reaction, gap and volume. This card adds an information source never used in the lab: the market-wide attention load of the reaction session (how many other liquid firms report the same session) and the end-of-week flag. The prediction is a slope change: the same reaction drifts more in its own direction when attention is scarce.","why_not_arbitraged":"Busy release sessions are the sessions when analysts, desks and liquidity providers are spread over the most names, so the capital and attention to correct each reaction is scarcest exactly then. They pay the overnight premium that later reverses.","why":"Firm-specific news that is not an SEC filing (analyst rating and target changes, media reports, third-party or regulator decisions) mostly reaches large US stocks outside trading hours, so it shows up as an overnight gap. Chan (2003) finds that large moves with a news headline drift on in the same direction, while large moves without news reverse. Womack (1996) finds drift after analyst recommendation changes, and it is larger after downgrades. The lab has tested filed news (H-0034, flat: the filing session can come days after the press release) and earnings news (drift, K-0046), but never news timed by the overnight gap itself. A gap is not always news, though. Berkman et al. (2012) show that attention-driven retail buying at the open inflates overnight returns, which then reverse. The claim is that the same gap is news (and drifts) or attention noise (and fades) depending on unsigned conditions that a taker can see at the close of the gap day: did the intraday session confirm or undo the gap, how heavy was the volume, how volatile and how covered is the name, and how far is the gap day from the last earnings release. Broad participation versus a thin print; unsigned.","Prior 21-session peer-residual return before the gap (signed). News with or against an existing move; separates underreaction from continuation of a running story.","63-session realized volatility of daily total returns (unsigned). Information uncertainty and limits to arbitrage; drift is expected to be larger where valuation is harder.","sp500_member at t (0/1, point-in-time extra). Coverage and passive ownership as a speed-of-incorporation proxy; unsigned.","Sessions since the last ea_reaction_day, capped at 63 (sec_8k_item202). A ridge on the same features can only add main effects: an unsigned feature moves up-gaps and down-gaps in the same direction, so it cannot flip or scale the response to the gap. Ridge collapses to 'continuation or fade proportional to zg and zi' for every row. A shallow tree ensemble can split on the sign of zg first and on the conditioners next. Who pays differs by branch: underreacting holders where the gap is news, attention buyers at the open where it is not. If ridge does as well, the claim is wrong and the card is a linear news-gap card that should be filed as such."},"notes":"FAMILY. The mechanism is underreaction to firm news. The lab's precedent for non-earnings news drift (H-0034, filed 8-K news) sits in post-earnings-announcement-drift, so this card is filed there too and its trial counts with H-0024, H-0028, H-0031, H-0033, H-0034, H-0095, H-0100, H-0101, H-0102 and H-0104. A new family name would escape that count. HOW IT DIFFERS from the cards it is closest to. H-0034 dated news by the 8-K filing session, which can trail the press release by days; this card dates news by the overnight gap and keeps only rows with NO filing, so the two event sets are disjoint by construction. H-0094 scored all rows on close-to-close own moves with earnings flags and had no overnight/intraday split. H-0100 used earnings-release rows only. This card excludes every earnings window. H-0103 (pending) is a weekly all-stock path-shape score for metaorder reversal; this card trains only on news-gap event rows and claims drift or fade conditional on unsigned conditioners. H-0030 is no-news close-to-close reversal. The mechanism test uses the gbm-vs-ridge disagreement design of K-0138, so the linear control the lab keeps asking for (K-0135, K-0141) runs inside G1. WHY THESE FEATURES. Every feature comes from the papers cited or from lab findings (K-0094 filing-timing caveat, H-0069 open pressure), not from a dev screen. No feature or threshold was picked by looking at results. FORECASTS (K-0120, K-0140: earlier Scout forecasts ran 2-4x too high). Candidates: peer-residual overnight gaps of 2.5 own-sigma happen on very roughly 1-3 % of member-days. Earnings windows hold a large share of them. After excluding earnings windows and filing sessions, I expect 0.6-1.5 % of member-days, i.e. 3-7 candidates per session, about 10000-23000 scored candidate rows over about 2007-2020 (the first two years go to the expanding training window). The gbm and ridge should disagree on 15-35 % of candidates: about 1500-8000 events on 1000-2500 dates. Round trip in LIQ-500 after 2001: about 10-12 bps (K-0140). Candidate gaps average about 3 %; if a tenth of the gap continues or reverses in the predicted direction, the gross per disagreement event is about 20-40 bps. A quarter of that, 5-10 bps, would sit below cost, and the card dies at the G1 cost check. That would mean: in large caps, overnight non-filed news carries no conditional drift or fade a next-open taker can collect. No follow-up card on the same events (no other threshold, hold or learner) should then be filed. BOOK ARITHMETIC (K-0098, K-0104). Weight 0.03 per slot, 5-session hold, 3-7 new slots per session: 15-35 open slots, slot gross 0.45-1.0 plus a small hedge, mean exposure about 0.5-0.9. Busy news days are scaled down by the gross cap. At about 1250 candidates a year, a net gain of 10 bps per slot gives about 3.5-4 % a year at about 5 % volatility (Sharpe about 0.7). I state this up front: a mechanism pass with gross near cost is not a strategy (K-0064). KNOWN LIMITS. (b) The 8-K datasets miss some CIKs and lean to survivors (K-0035), so some earnings gaps may leak into the candidate set. (c) G1 compares raw returns with unmarked peers (K-0074). (d) Per K-0134, no column or row subset may use end-of-view information. Run walk_forward on all columns with per-row membership and candidate masks; peers and medians are trailing only. (e) Liquid gap names may face a slightly worse cost tier than the average member.","references":[{"cite":"Chan, W. S. title: Capital-gains holding-period clock, learned - LIQ-500 market-neutral weekly: LightGBM scores stocks near the one-year tax anniversary of a stock-specific volume spike on gain x clock, hold 5 days

A supply bunch at the threshold shows in the first sessions; a slow build means momentum or reversal confounds, not tax selling.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below the T-bill bar (0.5) or a bootstrap bound of the difference below zero.","Neighbors of spike_mult 4, leg 0.2 or n_estimators 100: fewer than 75 % beat the benchmark, or doubled costs leave it below the bar.","Linear baseline: a ridge on the same five features, same rows, label and refit schedule, gives the same or a better net Sharpe than the gbm, so the sign-flip interaction is not what pays."],"family":"capital-gains-tax-timing","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Taxable individual investors (and tax-aware taxable accounts) who time sales to the holding-period threshold and accept a small price concession because the tax saving (15-20 percentage points of the gain) is far larger; liquidity providers who absorb the bunched supply earn the concession. The strategy is on the liquidity provider's side: short appreciated stocks as their pressure begins, long depreciated stocks as their pre-qualification selling ends.","why":"US tax law taxes gains on shares held more than one year at the long-term rate (15-20 % in 2004-2020) and gains on shares held one year or less at the ordinary rate (up to 35-39.6 %). A taxable holder who bought on a given day therefore defers selling an appreciated position until the day after its one-year anniversary and, conversely, realizes a losing position before it turns long-term (short-term losses offset income taxed at the higher rate; Constantinides 1984). When many shares change hands on one stock-specific day (a news-driven volume spike), the buyers of that day share one tax clock. One year later their tax-motivated trades bunch on known dates: supply of appreciated stock rises just after the qualification date (price pressure, then recovery), while supply of depreciated stock is front-loaded before it, so the pressure on losers ends at qualification. Reese (1998) found exactly this two-sided pattern around the long-term qualification date of IPO shares: appreciated stocks show more volume and lower returns just after qualification, depreciated stocks just before. The card asks whether the same clock, anchored on stock-specific volume spikes instead of IPO dates, is visible over 1-5 sessions in liquid US stocks, and lets a small walk-forward model learn the shape of the window instead of hand-tuning it on dev.","why_not_arbitraged":"It is not a mispricing that informed capital competes away but a predictable demand for immediacy that is rational for the seller. Each event is small, falls on an idiosyncratic date that has to be reconstructed from a purchase-day clock a year back, and is spread over hundreds of stocks a year; the concession per event is likely of the order of the trading cost, so capacity is small and dedicated capital uninterested."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of day t, a universe member crosses the long-term qualification date of its anchor spike (t is the first session with c >= 0, spike rule as in the signal with spike_mult): side -1 if g > 0 (appreciated, tax selling starts), side +1 if g < 0 (depreciated, pre-qualification selling ends); g = 0 is not an event.","horizons":[1,3,5,10,21],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["c: calendar days from the long-term qualification date (spike day + 366 days) of the stock's anchor spike, -14..+14 (the tax clock; from sharadar_sep dates)","g: cumulative log total return from the close of the spike day to the close of t (sign and size of the spike-day buyers' unrealized gain, which decides whether they wait for or run from the threshold)","log volume multiple of the spike day, dollar volume over its trailing 63-session median (how many shares carry this clock)","total return of the spike day (buyers chasing a jump versus buying a drop; a different clientele and gain profile)","63-session realized volatility of daily total returns at t (puts g in units of the stock's own risk)"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"The tax incentive changes sign at a threshold and depends on the sign of the gain: before qualification, holders of appreciated shares wait (supply withheld) and holders of depreciated shares sell (supply added); after qualification it is the reverse. The expected abnormal return is therefore roughly sign(g) x (1[c < 0] - 1[c >= 0]) scaled by the spike size, a product of a step in c and the sign of g whose main effects average to about zero over the window. A ridge on c, g, spike size, spike-day return and volatility can only add their effects and would see mainly the 12-month return in g (momentum); a tree splits on c near 0 and then on g. The width of the window and how large a gain must be to matter are unknown and would otherwise be tuned on dev; the model learns them walk-forward. The taxable sellers who bunch their sales at the threshold pay for it."},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks (liq_n 500), cross-sectional, 5-session label and hold, learned model. Why a new family: no card in the registry or the prior studies uses a holding-period tax clock; the closest relatives are the volume-attention cards (H-0014, H-0067, K-0024 avoid list) and earnings-date cards. This is not a volume-attention claim: the volume spike only dates a purchase, the predicted sign comes from the gain since that day and the side of the threshold, and nothing is traded on the spike itself. Earnings sessions are excluded around the spike so that the anniversary does not fall on next year's same-quarter release (H-0023 calendar), and market-wide volume days are excluded because index reconstitutions and expiries recur on the same calendar every year. Any recurring stock-specific annual event that does not depend on the sign of g is marked long and short in roughly equal measure and cancels in the side-adjusted average. Rivals and what they predict: 12-month momentum (g is close to a one-year return) works against the claim, since appreciated stocks are marked -1; a beta gap between appreciated and depreciated stocks (K-0074) moves with the market and should flip by third; generic short-term reversal is not a feature. Mechanism test design: the event is the rule the model has to learn (crossing of the qualification date, side from the sign of g), not the model's leg entries, because the lab's learned cards could never separate a wrong learner from an absent mechanism (K-0135, K-0142). A pass here with a failing book points at the learner or the book, a failure at the clock itself. Forecasts, written before any data (K-0120, K-0144): spike days roughly 400-900 a year in LIQ-500 after the exclusions (to be confirmed by G0 counts), so about 300-700 crossing events a year on most trading days, about 4000-9000 events on well over 1000 dates in dev from late 2005; window stocks per decision date roughly 20-60, legs of 4-12 names. Gross per crossing event: Reese's IPO setting (one shared purchase date, pre-1987, a heavily retail holder base) is the ceiling; in large caps most spike-day volume is institutional and much of it is tax-exempt, so the central forecast is 5-15 bps per event over 5 sessions against a round trip of about 11 bps, and at a tenth of the ceiling (1-3 bps) the card dies on cost. The book needs about 20 bps per leg entry or more to reach a net Sharpe of 0.5 with 10-25 names, so the most likely deaths are, in order: gross below cost at the mechanism test, a placebo percentile under the bar with few spikes per date, then the absolute Sharpe floor. (2) The sign of the skewness slope should flip with the source of the tail: a right tail made at an earnings release (ea21 = 1, onshare21 high) is news and drifts in its own direction (the lab's reaction-drift evidence), while a right tail made intraday without a release is lottery demand and gives back; a ridge can shift the level for ea21 but cannot flip the skew slope. (3) The left tail is non-monotone: moderately negative skew earns the crash premium, extremely negative skew with a large negative ret5 is a falling stock still in a sell-off. Journal of Financial Economics","year":2011}],"signal":{"description":"Decision dates: the first trading day of each week, after its close (data up to that close); trades at the open of the next trading day; positions held until the next weekly decision (about 5 sessions). title: Index-basket pressure in low-turnover S&P 500 members, learned - dollar-neutral 5-day cohorts after market-wide flow days, LightGBM on own move x inverse turnover

On a day of heavy market-wide basket flow the same dollar flow per unit of index weight hits every member, so the price impact per stock scales with weight divided by the stock's own dollar volume, i.e. with inverse turnover (market cap / dollar volume). Low-turnover members are therefore pushed beyond what their beta to the market implies on a flow day, high-turnover members less, and the non-fundamental part reverses over the following sessions as liquidity providers unwind. Ben-David, Franzoni and Moussawi (2018) show that stocks with more ETF ownership have more non-fundamental volatility and more negative return autocorrelation; Barberis, Shleifer and Wurgler (2005) show that index membership itself creates excess comovement. Within the S&P 500 the passive ownership share is roughly the same for every member, so the cross-sectional variation in basket pressure comes from inverse turnover, which is observable. This card is the separation test the lab asked for after H-0106/H-0107 (K-0148): is the flow-day reversal generic stress rebound, which should not depend on inverse turnover once beta and the own move are controlled, or basket pressure, which should be concentrated where index trading is a large share of a stock's volume?","why_not_arbitraged":"The concession per stock is small, lasts days, and sits on market-wide stress-or-euphoria days when liquidity-providing capital is scarce and risk limits bind; the trade needs short positions on hundreds of names at once. The predicted 5-day return of a member is roughly minus (own move - beta x market move) x inverse turnover, larger on high basket-volume days, with the sign set by the direction of the market move. In a cross-sectional ranking a ridge cannot use the two date-level features at all (they shift every member equally), and its inverse-turnover coefficient is a static low-turnover tilt that the same-stock placebo absorbs; it can express only plain reversal and a beta tilt. A small tree ensemble can condition the reversal slope on inverse turnover and on the size and sign of the flow day. Who pays: basket traders who trade every member in index proportions on flow days and pay the concession in low-turnover names; the reversal is the liquidity providers' compensation. If the ridge picks earn as much as the gbm-only picks, the interaction is absent and what remains is ordinary reversal (K-0133)."},"notes":"Why this is not a retry. Here the flow day is market-wide by construction and the separating variable is cross-sectional: inverse turnover, the observable intensity of basket pressure per stock, with beta and the own move as controls, and the mechanism event is the gbm-versus-ridge disagreement design of K-0142, so the linear control runs inside G1 (K-0135). Both sides are marked on both up and down flow days, so the market's own rebound after down days cancels to first order; a residual beta gap between gbm-only longs and shorts (K-0074) is the main confound and is not neutralized by G1. Forecasts, written before any run (K-0120, K-0151): flow days at 1.5 sigma about 12-15 % of sessions (about 30-38 per year, 500-650 dates over 2003-2020); gbm-only picks per side per flow day about 30-50 of the 100 top-fifth names, so roughly 30000-60000 events. Round trip in the S&P 500 about 12-14 bps (H-0106 measured 13.5). Gross per event: central 10-15 bps (below the 28 bps H-0106 measured for all flow-day entries, since the disagreement set is narrower), pessimistic 3 bps (K-0151: Scout forecasts have run 3-10x high). At the central case the cost ratio is about 1 and the book would be marginal; at the pessimistic case it dies at the cost check, which still answers the lab question if the placebo percentile is read: inverse turnover adds timing information or it does not. Book arithmetic: cohort gross 0.5 on about 35 flow days a year with a 5-session hold gives mean gross exposure about 0.3 (clusters capped at 1.0). They trade the share updates at the rebalance close whatever the price, and pay a concession to the liquidity providers and pre-positioners who take the other side in the days before.","why":"Cap-weighted index funds hold each S&P 500 member in proportion to its index share count. A member whose shares outstanding rose since the last update (stock compensation, small issuance, conversions) must be bought by every passive tracker at that close, and one whose share count shrank (buybacks) must be sold. So price pressure should build in the days before the rebalance close, in the direction of the pending share change and scaled by the trade size in days of volume, and should partly reverse afterwards. The claim here is an additive concession that is already selected by restricting the universe to the volatile half. Holding period: every position is decided anew each week for the next 5 sessions, which is what the 5-day label predicts (typical_days 5 = label horizon); because of the buffer a name can be re-decided into the same leg, so a stock's run in a leg averages about 8-12 sessions, made of consecutive 5-session decisions. New leg entries per week about 15-25 in total, so about 1050 weekly decisions from about 2000 give 15000-25000 events on about 1000 dates. Gross Sharpe forecast: central 0.7 (H-0115 gross cleared 0.5, beta neutrality should remove some short-leg loss), pessimistic 0.35, and about 0 if the H-0115 pass was the volatile half's market exposure; net central 0.4, which is under the floor, so the most likely death is the same absolute Sharpe floor at G1, now with the cost drag and the beta gap removed as excuses. a wrong-signed latest third is a kill condition for the card even if the pooled test passes (K-0060).","Mechanism shape: if the 10- and 21-session abnormal returns are much larger than the 5-session one (slow drift rather than a release within a few weeks of the deadline), the tax-pressure reading is refuted.","Net Sharpe on dev below 0.5 or not above T-bill + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the difference below zero.","Neighbors of n_estimators 100 or leg 0.1: fewer than 75 % beat the benchmark.","A ridge on the same features with the same schedule and book (framework ridge) gives the same or a better result: then the deadline interaction is not what pays (the ridge can only hold a static loser or winner tilt inside the windows)."],"family":"capital-gains-tax-timing","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Tax-motivated sellers (funds before their October year end, individuals before December 31) who accept a price concession because the tax value of realizing the loss before the deadline exceeds it, and who cannot rebuy for 30 days; liquidity providers that absorb the seasonal supply are paid the rebound.","why":"Two groups of holders face a hard tax deadline for realizing losses: US mutual funds, whose excise-tax year ends with October (they must distribute gains realized through the end of October, so they harvest losses before it), and taxable individuals, whose year ends with December. Before each deadline these holders sell stocks in which they sit on losses (losses measured over THEIR tax year and against their purchase prices), and the wash-sale rule keeps them from buying the same stock back for 30 days. This is a predictable, non-informational supply that should push loss stocks down relative to other stocks in the weeks before the deadline, and its end (plus the delayed repurchases) should let them rebound in the weeks after it (Gibson, Safieddine and Titman 2000 for the October fund deadline; Grinblatt and Moskowitz 2004 for December losers and the January rebound). Whether a recent move reverts or persists therefore depends on where it was made and who traded it, not on its size alone.","why_not_arbitraged":"Market makers in altcoins are capital- and inventory-constrained, the trade needs a short leg in perps with funding risk, the edge per coin is small relative to altcoin volatility and taker costs, and it lives in a 24/7 market split across time zones where no single desk sees all sessions as one book."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"A coin enters the top fifth of the gbm score (side +1) or the bottom fifth (side -1) at a decision date, i.e. it was not in that leg at the previous decision date.","horizons":[1,3,5,10,20],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["Asia-session BTC-residual return over the last 3 days (flow-driven, retail-hours component of the recent move)","Europe-session BTC-residual return over the last 3 days (intermediate clientele; control for the session split)","US-session BTC-residual return over the last 3 days (component made while US investors and US news are active)","Abnormal US-session volume share (US participation in the recent move, against the coin's own month)","Realized-volatility state, 7-day vs 60-day hourly realized vol (how stressed the coin's market is; concession size)","Trailing 3-day funding (price of leverage; crowding of the longs that make Asian-session moves)"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"A ridge on the three session returns can already give each session its own sign, so the card claims less than a session split: it claims that the sign and size of the response to a session's move depend on the US volume share and on the volatility state. The lab has seen both halves separately in liquid US stocks (no-news moves revert: H-0030, H-0115; moves on information-rich earnings releases drift: H-0028, H-0033) but never a stock-level measure of how informed the trading between releases is. No date literals in the strategy; the data period is set at the 8-K dataset start so that no feature is blank in the first block.","references":[{"cite":"Llorente, Michaely, Saar, Wang (2002) Dynamic Volume-Return Relation of Individual Stocks, Review of Financial Studies","year":2002},{"cite":"Campbell, Grossman, Wang (1993) Trading Volume and Serial Correlation in Stock Returns, Quarterly Journal of Economics","year":1993},{"cite":"Aboody, Lev (2000) Information Asymmetry, R&D, and Insider Gains, Journal of Finance","year":2000}],"signal":{"description":"Data per stock j and session t, all known after the close of t. r = (1 + ret_co)(1 + ret_oc) - 1 (close-to-close total return); e[t,j] = r[t,j] minus the equal-weight mean r of the LIQ-500 members of t (residual return); sigma[t,j] = standard deviation of e over the last 63 sessions (at least 40 valid). title: Round-number support and resistance, learned - LIQ-500 dollar-neutral daily, LightGBM on the unadjusted close's place on the dollar grid, 1-day hold; mechanism = gbm-only vs ridge picks
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","description":"LIQ-500 point-in-time members; close_u (unadjusted) is a signal input here, P&L uses total returns only.","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","close_u","dollar_volume","tradable"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2001-05-01","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the gbm-only leg entries (event below) earn a one-session side-adjusted abnormal return under the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or a gross per event below the round-trip cost (expected about 11 bps in LIQ-500).","Mechanism, decay: the latest third of the dev period has the wrong sign (K-0060). This is a kill even if the pooled test passes.","Nonlinearity: if the disagreement average is negative (the ridge's own leg picks beat the gbm's own picks), the round-number grid adds nothing beyond linear reversal and volatility, and the card is refuted, not 'cannot tell'.
