Limit orders (take-profit, stop and plain resting orders, largely retail) cluster at whole dollars, and more so at $5, $10, $50 and $100 levels. Liquidity demanders with left-digit bias buy just below round numbers and sell just above them (Bhattacharya, Holden and Jacobsen 2012, over 100 million US trades). The resting buy orders at the round number just below a close support the price during the next session, and the resting sell orders at the round number just above cap it. Stocks that close just above a round number should therefore beat stocks that close just below one over the next session. Zhang (2024) reports this next-day spread in US stocks. The price information is the UNADJUSTED close: that is the number traders see, and no input the lab has tested so far uses it. The claim here is that the effect is (a) still present in the most liquid 500 stocks, (b) still there when entering at the next open rather than the close, and (c) large enough per entry to pay a taker's round trip.","why_not_arbitraged":"The edge per stock is a few to a few dozen basis points over one session. Harvesting it needs a full daily rotation of a broad book, which taker costs largely eat. Market makers who see the order book capture part of it intraday, but they carry inventory limits and do not hold overnight positions sized to the level. The behaviour behind it is a stable cognitive bias, not a strategy that crowds out."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"A LIQ-500 member enters the gbm's long leg (side +1) or short leg (side -1) after the close of day t, i.e. it is in the top (bottom) `top` fraction of the gbm score on t and was not in that leg on t-1, AND the ridge control on the same features does not place it in the same leg on t. These are the picks only the nonlinear model makes, which should be the round-number-grid picks.","horizons":[1,2,5],"primary_horizon_days":1},"ml":{"features":["cents_off - signed distance of the unadjusted close to the nearest whole dollar, in dollars (raw); where on the round-number grid the close sits","roundness - 0/1/2/3 for an ordinary dollar, multiple of 5, of 10, of 50 (raw); how much limit-order clustering to expect at the nearest level","log unadjusted close (z-scored); the same cents matter more for a low-priced stock, and whole dollars are not salient for high-priced ones","crossing - +1/-1/0 if today's close crossed the nearest level upward/downward (raw, 0 on split days); a level just crossed becomes support or resistance","one-day total return (z-scored); control so that generic one-day reversal is not read as a grid effect","21-day realized volatility of daily total returns (z-scored); scales how much of the next session's range the level can hold"],"horizon_days":1,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"The claimed effect is a step at the round number. A close one cent above a salient level is supported, one cent below is capped, and the effect dies out toward the middle of the grid. On the cents_off axis it is a sawtooth: positive just above zero, negative just below, about zero near +/-0.50, where a close of +0.49 and one of -0.51 sit equally far from the next level. Its height should grow with roundness and fall with the price level. A ridge on the same six features can only draw a straight line in cents_off. That line wrongly calls +0.49 the strongest long and -0.49 the strongest short. It also cannot make the step depend on roundness, price or a crossing today, so the ridge's legs will be driven mostly by one-day reversal and volatility. A tree can place a split at cents_off = 0 and condition it on the other features. The left-digit-biased liquidity demanders and the clustered limit orders at the level pay for it."},"notes":"Why this is not a near-copy of earlier lab work: it is the first card whose information is the price LEVEL (the unadjusted close on the dollar grid). Every earlier stock card used returns, volume, fundamentals, filings or calendars. The one-day return is in the feature set as a control, and the event keeps only picks the ridge does not make, so the generic reversal of the short-term-reversal family (H-0030, H-0094, H-0115) is netted out by design rather than re-tested. It is not 52-week-high anchoring (H-0011, H-0083) either: the reference is a fixed price grid common to all stocks, not a stock's own history, and the claim is about the next session, not weeks. Family: a new name because the mechanism is order clustering on a fixed grid (microstructure plus left-digit bias), not drift or anchoring to own history. If the Chair prefers to file it under 52-week-high-anchoring, the card accepts that. Period: the data period starts 2001-05-01 because US equities quoted in 1/16 and 1/8 ticks until decimalization was completed in April 2001. Before that the 'one cent above/below a round number' grid did not exist, and costs carry a x2.5 pre-decimal factor. This date comes from market structure, not from returns. The dev thirds are then about 2001-2007, 2007-2014 and 2014-2020. Timing caveat, stated up front: the literature measures close-to-close, while the lab enters at the next open. If the support acts through the resting orders during the next session, open-to-open keeps most of it. If the overnight gap already moves the price away from the level, it is lost. The 1-session horizon tests exactly this. Forecast (K-0120, K-0144, K-0159, K-0165): the event is model-defined, so counts are uncertain. Each day about 50 names per leg, perhaps 60-80 % of them new (grid positions change daily), and perhaps a third to a half not shared with the ridge. That gives a central 20-40 events a day, about 80000-180000 over roughly 4700 scored dates. At a call rate a tenth of that there would still be well over 200 events on 30 dates. Round trip in LIQ-500 is about 11 bps (K-0165). Gross per event: central 3 bps, optimistic 12 bps, mechanism-absent case 0 or below. The published spread is about 25 bps a day across all US stocks, dominated by low-priced small names, and large caps should carry a fraction of it. The likeliest death is therefore the G1 cost check: a real but sub-cost effect. With this many events the placebo bar should lie well under cost, so a failure is a real 'not tradable for a taker', not a power problem. Book arithmetic (K-0064, K-0098): gross 1.0 always, mean exposure about 1.0. With daily leg turnover of about 70 %, cost drag is roughly 252 x 0.7 x 11 bps, near 19 % a year. The book can clear a 0.5 net Sharpe only if gross per new entry is about 15 bps or more, above the optimistic case. A mechanism pass with gross between 11 and 15 bps would still fail the strategy gate. That outcome would show a real round-number effect that only a maker could harvest.","references":[{"cite":"Bhattacharya, Holden, Jacobsen (2012) Penny Wise, Dollar Foolish: Buy-Sell Imbalances On and Around Round Numbers, Management Science 58(2)","year":2012},{"cite":"Zhang (2024) Above Up, Below Down: The Impact of Limit Order Clustering on Stock Price Movements, SSRN working paper","year":2024}],"signal":{"description":"Data: sharadar_sep stocks, point-in-time LIQ-500 members, from the card's data period start (after US decimalization). Decision after the close of day t using data up to that close; trades at the open of t+1. Total daily return r_t = (1 + ret_co_t) * (1 + ret_oc_t) - 1 (ret_co = previous close to open, ret_oc = open to close). P_t = close_u (unadjusted close). Features per stock and date (six): (1) cents_off = P_t - round(P_t) in dollars, in [-0.50, +0.50): the signed distance to the nearest whole dollar (positive = just above it); (2) roundness of that nearest whole-dollar level L = round(P_t): 3 if L is a multiple of 50, else 2 if a multiple of 10, else 1 if a multiple of 5, else 0; (3) log(P_t); (4) crossing = +1 if close_u_{t-1} < L <= P_t (the level was crossed upward today), -1 if close_u_{t-1} >= L > P_t (crossed downward), else 0. Set it to 0 when close_u_t / close_u_{t-1} differs from 1 + r_t by more than 1 % (a split or other corporate action moved the unadjusted price); (5) r_t, the one-day total return (control for one-day reversal); (6) 21-day realized volatility of r (control for how far the price can travel relative to the grid). Features 1, 2 and 4 are positions on an absolute price grid and are passed raw. Features 3, 5 and 6 are z-scored across the members of the date with the framework helper. A member with any missing feature is not scored. Label: total return from the open of t+1 to the open of t+2 (horizon_days 1), ranked across members on each date (framework label). Model: LightGBM (framework gbm), num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 200, other settings framework default, n_estimators from params, expanding window, refit every 63 rows through lab.framework.ml.walk_forward (its purge and minimum training sample). Book (score_weights): each decision day, long the top `top` fraction of scored members by gbm score and short the bottom `top` fraction, equal weight within each leg, 0.5 gross per leg (dollar-neutral, gross 1.0), held to the next decision. title: Macro-cleaned liquidity concession, learned - LIQ-500 beta-neutral weekly, ridge on 5-day returns split into a cross-asset ETF part and a residual, hold 5 days
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","description":"LIQ-500 point-in-time members, total returns and dollar volume; start after the last factor ETF (UUP) has listed","frequency":"1d","period":["2007-03-01","2020-12-31"]},{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","description":"Signal only, never traded: equity market, Treasuries, gold, commodity index and dollar factor returns for the per-stock exposure regressions","frequency":"1d","instruments":["SPY","IEF","GLD","DBC","UUP"],"period":["2007-03-01","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: new entries into the long and short fifths of the ridge score do not beat the 95th percentile of time-shifted placebos at 5 sessions, or their gross side-adjusted abnormal return is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the latest third of the dev window has the opposite sign to the pooled average (decay, K-0060), or fewer than two thirds share the sign.","Mechanism shape: the effect is largest at 10 sessions and still growing (slow drift), rather than building over the first sessions and easing by 10 (a concession).","Net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or not above T-bills + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the difference below zero.","Neighbors of top 0.2 or beta_days 252 fail the benchmark in more than a quarter of cases, or the median neighbor Sharpe is below 0.7 of the primary.","Doubled costs leave net Sharpe below the T-bill bar.","Cross-asset claim: a ridge on the plain market-adjusted 5-day and 21-day returns (beta to SPY only, same vol and volume features, same schedule) gives the same or a better entry gross; then the information from the other markets adds nothing and the card is plain reversal.","Cross-asset claim: the ridge weight on the cross-asset part of the move is as negative as the weight on the non-macro residual (both revert), so the split carries no information."],"family":"short-term-reversal","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Traders who demand immediacy in a single stock for reasons unrelated to macro news (fund redemptions and inflows, index and risk rebalancing, stop and margin selling) and accept a temporary price concession; the liquidity provider who buys their sales and sells into their purchases for about a week collects it.","why":"A weekly stock move has two parts with different futures. The part explained by the stock's exposure to other markets (Treasury yields, gold, commodities, the dollar) is public macro news that is priced by macro investors and should not revert (the lab's only cross-asset stock pass, H-0114, even found a delayed continuation for oil). The part left after removing the market and the cross-asset factors is mostly non-macro order flow: fire sales, rebalancing and impatient trades in a single name, for which liquidity providers demand a price concession that reverts over days. Da, Liu and Schaumburg (2014) show that returns unexplained by fundamental news reverse far more than raw returns. A plain market-adjusted reversal sort mixes the two parts, so it fades informed macro moves in energy, miners, rate-sensitive and dollar-sensitive names and dilutes the concession. Using the other markets to clean the move should concentrate the book on the non-macro concession, which is the claim tested here.","why_not_arbitraged":"Liquidity provision ties up capital in volatile names and its payoff is a small spread per trade that is roughly the size of trading costs; market makers hold inventory for minutes, not a week, and statistical arbitrage capital is scarce exactly when concessions are largest. The usual explanation is slow diffusion of coin-specific news among attention-constrained retail holders who arrive late and chase winners. Momentum also has a known failure state (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016): after a broad sell-off in a high-volatility \"panic\" state, the loser leg is mostly high-beta names marked down with the market, not names with bad news, and it rebounds sharply when the pressure stops. This card claims that a signal from another market, US equity implied volatility (VIX), tells the two cases apart for crypto. When US implied volatility is high, crypto weakness is largely caused by cross-asset deleveraging (multi-asset funds, leveraged traders meeting margin calls elsewhere, risk-parity style cuts), which sells high-beta coins regardless of their own news. So a coin's three-week underperformance then says little about the coin, and losers should revert relative to winners. When US implied volatility is low and crypto still moved, the moves are crypto-specific information and momentum should continue. A walk-forward gradient-boosted model on four coin features plus two date-level state variables (VIX level and BTC trend) is asked to learn which sign the momentum slope has in which state.","why_not_arbitraged":"Crypto long/short needs perps with funding costs, coin-level jump risk and exchange risk. Most crypto-native capital does not watch US option-implied volatility, and most TradFi capital cannot short altcoins. The claim is that the sign of the momentum slope depends on the cross-asset state: in calm US states recent winners keep winning (slow diffusion of coin news, paid by late chasers), in high-VIX states with a falling BTC the three-week losers are high-beta coins sold indiscriminately by cross-asset deleveragers and they revert (paid by the forced sellers and by momentum traders short the loser leg). Its lesson and K-0119 report a continuation shape at 5-10 days in liquid perps, which is the default this card builds on: formation over three weeks, momentum by default, with the US state as a learned switch of the sign rather than a gate on a reversal trade. Family short-term-momentum (H-0029) because the features are momentum features; not cross-sectional-momentum (12-1 month stock sleeves). Study 9's long-only weekly altcoin momentum on 2022-2026 is a different book (long-only, no state, holdout years); it is related and counts against this family's prior. K-0162 found date-level states useless for learned stock sorts; this card tests the same question in a market where the state comes from outside it, and states the descriptive check of whether the model used the state. New leg entries per day about 1-1.5 per leg, so about 1500-2500 events on 600-850 dates (pessimistic 1000). Features per coin and day, from the coin's own perp total returns (all windows end at the close of t): (1) ret_21 = total return over the last 21 days; (2) ret_5 = total return over the last 5 days; (3) vol_30 = standard deviation of daily log returns over the last 30 days; (4) beta_60 = OLS slope of the coin's daily returns on BTCUSDT.P daily returns over the last 60 days (BTC itself = 1). This card does not sort on the premium at all: it marks rare Korea-specific VOLUME surges that come with a Binance up-move (the transmitted pump), one side only, and claims overreaction rather than underreaction. title: Credit-market news into levered equities, learned - LIQ-500 beta-neutral legs in weeks of a credit-specific Baa spread move, LightGBM on leverage x shock, hold 5 days
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity","macro"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"sharadar_sf1","fields":["sf1_arq_debt","sf1_arq_marketcap","sf1_art_ebit","sf1_art_intexp"],"frequency":"1q"},{"dataset":"fred_moody_yields_1d","description":"Moody's seasoned Baa corporate yield, signal only (clock next_morning)","fields":["DBAA"],"frequency":"1d"},{"dataset":"fred_macro","description":"10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield, signal only (clock next_morning)","fields":["DGS10"],"frequency":"1d"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return of the leg entries on credit-news dates does not exceed the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or its gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism decay: the latest third of dev has the wrong sign (K-0060), even if the pooled test passes.","Mechanism shape: the 1- and 3-session averages are about zero or wrong-signed and the effect appears only at 20 sessions; that is a slow leverage style drift, not diffusion of credit news within the week.","Linear baseline: a ridge (framework ridge) on the same six features, same training rows, label and refit schedule gives the same or a larger event gross; then the convexity claim is false.","Strategy: net Sharpe below 0.5, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference to T-bills at or below zero, or net Sharpe at 2x costs not above T-bills.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbors of z_news 1.0 and n_estimators 100 beat the benchmark, or one third of dev carries more than 60 % of the log return."],"family":"oil-shock-equity-underreaction","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Equity investors in levered firms who trade on equity-market information only (equity mandates, analysts who follow earnings, not the bond market) and keep buying or holding levered stocks at prices that have not absorbed the credit market's repricing of default risk; after tightening, those who sell levered names too cheaply.","why":"The equity of a levered firm is a call on its assets (Merton 1974): its value depends on credit conditions, and the dependence is small for low-leverage firms and steep near default (high debt relative to equity value, high equity volatility, thin interest coverage). When the corporate bond market reprices default risk by more than the stock market and Treasuries explain (a credit-specific widening or tightening of the Moody's Baa yield over the 10-year Treasury), that is news about the value of levered equity that equity-only investors do not watch. Equity and credit markets are often out of line because their investor bases are separate and arbitrage between them is limited (Kapadia and Pu 2012). The claim: in the week after a large credit-specific spread move, highly levered, low-coverage, volatile stocks move in the direction the credit news implies (down after widening, up after tightening) relative to stocks of the same market beta, and the response is concentrated in that corner of the balance-sheet space, which the model is asked to find.","why_not_arbitraged":"Capital-structure arbitrage desks trade single-name CDS against single-name equity, not an aggregate credit index against a balance-sheet cross-section; the signal is a macro credit move that needs a cross-market mandate, it fires in a minority of weeks, and its legs carry idiosyncratic and crash risk (levered stocks), so it is capital-intensive and lumpy. Kapadia and Pu relate equity-credit dislocation to exactly these impediments (idiosyncratic risk, liquidity, investor heterogeneity)."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"On a credit-news decision date (first session of a week with |credit-shock z| >= z_news), a stock enters the long leg (side +1) or the short leg (side -1) of the book: the top or bottom tenth of the gbm score within its tercile of 252-session market beta.","horizons":[1,3,5,10,20],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["Market leverage: quarterly total debt (sf1_arq_debt) over debt plus equity value (sf1_arq_marketcap at the filing, rolled forward with the stock's total return); the Merton exposure of equity to credit conditions","Interest coverage: TTM EBIT over TTM interest expense (sf1_art_ebit, sf1_art_intexp), winsorized; near-term debt-service capacity, which decides whether a spread move is about this firm","Equity volatility: 63-session realized volatility of daily total returns; with leverage it forms a distance to default (Bharath-Shumway style), the convexity of equity to credit","Signed leverage: market leverage times the credit-shock z (residual 5-session change of Baa minus 10y Treasury after the equal-weight stock market and the 10y yield); the direction in which the credit news pushes a levered equity","Own response: the stock's return over the shock window minus beta times the market; whether the levered name has already priced the credit news (the underreaction gap)","Market beta: 252-session beta to the equal-weight LIQ-500 return; separates leverage from market exposure (K-0074); legs are also built within beta terciles"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":252,"why_not_linear":"Merton equity is convex in firm value: its sensitivity to credit conditions is near zero for the many low-leverage, investment-grade members and rises steeply only where leverage is high AND equity volatility is high AND coverage is thin, and only if the stock has not already moved (own response near zero or against the news). That is a three- or four-way corner. A ridge on the same six features applies one slope on signed leverage to the whole cross-section, so its legs are filled with levered but safe names (utilities, financially strong issuers) where the credit news is irrelevant, and it cannot switch the slope off where the stock already responded. The gbm can isolate the corner. If the ridge on the same rows, label and schedule does as well, the claim that convexity pays is false and what remains is a plain leverage sort signed by the credit shock. The payer is the equity-only holder of a near-distress levered stock who does not read the bond market."},"notes":"Why this is not a rerun of H-0116 (same family, counted there on purpose: exposure to a macro shock, delayed stock response): H-0116 pooled rate, dollar and credit shocks and mapped stocks to them with one-year statistical betas, which its lesson calls noisy; its open question was an explicit economic mapping. This card uses credit only, maps stocks by balance sheet (market leverage, coverage, volatility; Merton) instead of a return regression, measures the shock as the Baa-minus-Treasury move not explained by the stock market and by Treasuries (so it is not equity stress, K-0084), and builds the legs within beta terciles (K-0074). K-0164 asks why the series is clean and the link large: Moody's yields are market-based daily averages (not revised), and the link is structural for exactly the corner the model targets; for the rest of LIQ-500 it is small, which is why the card is a learned corner and not a linear sort. Dev-seen motivation, stated for the Skeptic: H-0080 found credit ETFs kept falling after credit-specific residual drops (wrong sign for its reversal claim); that hints credit-specific news persists, but it is a different claim on different instruments, not evidence for this card. Forecasts (K-0098, K-0120, K-0165): |z| >= 1 on a fat-tailed residual should mark about 20-30 % of weeks. Scoring starts after the 252-session shock warm-up plus 40 news dates of training (about 2001-2002), so about 950-1000 weeks remain and 200-300 news dates; with about 450-480 scored members, 2 x 10 % legs give about 90 entries per date, 18000 to 27000 events. The first third of dev (to mid-2005) holds only its last 3-4 years of scores (K-0163), including the 2001-2002 credit episode. Round trip about 11-12 bps (LIQ-500 tiers, K-0171). Gross per event: central 6 bps (any effect in large caps is small), optimistic 25 bps, pessimistic zero or below (credit-specific moves are bond-market liquidity, not news, and levered stocks do nothing). Mean exposure by the K-0104 formula: about 22000 entries x 5 sessions / 5800 sessions x about 0.011 weight = 0.21-0.27, close to the floor of 0.20; a thinner news share would fail it. Likeliest death: the mechanism gross stays under cost (central case); next, a pass whose part-time book misses the absolute Sharpe floor (K-0027, as H-0114). If it dies, the lab learns whether credit news reaches levered large caps within a week at all, which neither H-0116 nor H-0080 could say. The ridge control: please report the ridge event gross and percentile next to the gbm's if the framework can (K-0135); the card's convexity claim depends on it.","references":[{"cite":"Merton (1974) On the Pricing of Corporate Debt: The Risk Structure of Interest Rates, Journal of Finance","year":1974},{"cite":"Kapadia and Pu (2012) Limited arbitrage between equity and credit markets, Journal of Financial Economics 105(3)","year":2012}],"signal":{"description":"Data: LIQ-500 point-in-time members (sharadar_sep total returns from ret_co and ret_oc), quarterly and TTM fundamentals from sharadar_sf1 (usable from the day after the filing, as the loader delivers them), Moody's Baa yield DBAA (fred_moody_yields_1d) and the 10-year Treasury yield DGS10 (fred_macro), both with clock next_morning, so at the close of day t the latest usable values are those of day t-1 or earlier. (1) Market return: the equal-weight mean daily total return of the LIQ-500 members of each day (no ETF needed). (2) Credit shock, date-level, computed at the close of each decision day t: spread S = DBAA - DGS10 (last value at or before t-1; if either series has no new value for more than 5 sessions, no shock that day). dS = change of S over the 5 sessions ending t-1; dY = change of DGS10 over the same 5 sessions; M = compounded equal-weight market return over the same 5 sessions. Regress dS on M and dY over the trailing 252 sessions of such overlapping 5-session windows (ending at t-1, OLS with intercept); the credit shock is today's residual divided by the standard deviation of the trailing 252 residuals (z). Needs 252 sessions of history, so the first shock is about a year after the data start. Positive z = credit-specific widening. (3) Decision dates: the first trading session of each week. A decision date is a credit-news date when |z| >= z_news. Only credit-news dates are used for training and trading. (4) Features per stock and decision date, each z-scored across that date's members by the framework helper (stocks with any missing feature are not scored): (a) market leverage = sf1_arq_debt / (sf1_arq_debt + E), where E = sf1_arq_marketcap of the latest usable filing rolled forward with the stock's compounded total return since the first session that filing was usable; missing debt counts as 0, missing marketcap means not scored; (b) interest coverage = sf1_art_ebit / sf1_art_intexp, winsorized to [-5, 30]; interest expense missing or <= 0 gives 30; (c) equity volatility = standard deviation of the last 63 daily total returns; (d) signed leverage = market leverage x z (the helper's cross-sectional z-scoring keeps its sign and ranking: levered names point in the direction of the credit news); (e) own response = the stock's compounded total return over the same 5 sessions as the shock window plus day t, minus its beta x the market return over those sessions; (f) beta = OLS slope of the stock's daily total return on the market return over the last 252 sessions (at least 200 valid days, else not scored). (5) Label (framework): total return from the next open to the open 5 sessions later, ranked across members. (6) Model: lab.framework.ml.walk_forward with model gbm (LightGBM), num_leaves 15, learning_rate 0.05, min_child_samples 200, n_estimators as in params; trained only on rows of credit-news decision dates whose labels are fully realized by the decision date (framework purge), expanding window, refit every 252 rows, framework seeds. The first fit needs at least 40 credit-news dates of training rows; before that nothing is scored or traded. Run on all columns and mask non-members per row (no ever-member column list, K-0134). (7) Book (score_weights, only_on credit-news dates): split scored members into terciles of feature (f) beta; in each tercile take the top tenth of the score long and the bottom tenth short (rounded down, at least 3 names per side per tercile, else that tercile is skipped). Equal weight: the long names share +0.5, the short names -0.5 (gross 1.0, dollar-neutral, beta balanced by construction). Enter at the next open, hold to the next weekly decision (5 sessions), then close; on a decision date that is not a credit-news date the book is flat. A stock that leaves the universe during the hold is closed at the first decision row outside the universe (K-0051). Fewer than 60 scored members on a news date means flat.","params":{"n_estimators":{"grid":[50,100,200],"value":100},"z_news":{"grid":[0.75,1.0,1.5],"value":1.0}},"timeframes":["1d","1w"]},"title":"Credit-market news into levered equities, learned - LIQ-500 beta-neutral legs in weeks of a credit-specific Baa spread move, LightGBM on leverage x shock, hold 5 days","universe":{"kind":"liq_n","n":500}}

title: Treasury auction supply cycle, peer-testable - short TLT/IEF 3 sessions before each 5y-30y auction cluster, long 3 after, short-Treasury ETFs as peers

{"asset_classes":["us_etf"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","description":"TLT and IEF traded; SHY, SHV, BIL, VGSH, SCHO as unmarked short-Treasury peers. Start after BIL lists (2007-05) so that at least three unmarked peers exist on every event date (K-0086).","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2007-07-02","2020-12-31"]},{"dataset":"treasury_auctions_1d","description":"Auction calendar of nominal 5y/7y/10y/20y/30y coupon auctions (new issues and reopenings), signal only.","fields":["next_coupon5_sessions","last_coupon5_sessions"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2007-07-02","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 3-session abnormal return of TLT/IEF against the short-Treasury peers is not above the 95th percentile of the 200 time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost of TLT/IEF: there is no tradable auction cycle in Treasury ETF prices.","Mechanism decay (K-0060): the latest third of the event window (about 2016-2020) has the wrong sign. Declared kill condition even if the pooled test passes.","Horizon shape: if the abnormal return is near zero at 1-3 sessions and only grows toward 10 sessions, the result is generic duration drift, not a supply concession that reverses within the week; the card is then wrong even if the percentile clears.","If a by-phase split is reported: either phase (PRE short or POST long) wrong-signed on its own means the cycle claim is wrong and the pooled number is one-sided drift.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or below the T-bill Sharpe + 0.10, or the 75 % bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference to T-bills not above zero.","Robustness: the neighbors hold_sessions 2 and 4 do not beat T-bills, or doubled costs leave Sharpe below the T-bill benchmark, or more than 60 % of the log return comes from one third of dev."],"family":"treasury-auction-supply-concession","holding_period":{"rebalance":"event","typical_days":3},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"End investors who buy duration at the auction or just after it at a concession (real-money accounts that need the new on-the-run issue for benchmark reasons, foreign official buyers), and the dealers who must hold inventory through the auction and are paid the concession for it. The strategy is on the dealers' side of the trade: it sells duration before supply arrives and buys it after, i.e. it supplies a little of the risk-bearing capacity that is scarce around auctions.","why":"The US Treasury sells a pre-announced, large amount of 5- to 30-year coupon debt in clusters twice a month (10y/30y around mid-month, 5y/7y around month-end). Primary dealers must absorb most of each auction and then distribute it to end investors who arrive slowly. Because dealers have limited risk-bearing capacity and end investors' capital is not perfectly mobile, dealers and other short-horizon holders reduce duration in the days before the auction to make room (and short in when-issued trading), which pushes long Treasury prices down; once the supply is placed and gradually distributed, prices recover over the following days. Lou, Yan and Zhang (2013) document exactly this cycle in the secondary market (prices fall in the few days before, recover shortly after, even though dates and sizes are announced) and tie it to dealer capacity. Long-duration Treasury ETFs (TLT, IEF) hold the same securities and are priced by APs against them, so the concession should show in their prices; short-Treasury ETFs (SHY, SHV, BIL, VGSH, SCHO) hold bills and 1-3y notes that are not part of these auctions and serve as unmarked peers.","why_not_arbitraged":"The concession is the price of inventory risk on very large sizes: a few basis points of yield on tens of billions per auction. Arbitrage capital that could absorb it faces duration risk several times larger than the expected gain per cycle, balance-sheet costs (post-2008 leverage ratio limits on dealers) and a payoff that is small per event, so it is only partly competed away. The paper estimates an issuance cost of 9-18 bps of the auction size, i.e. the effect survived in the most liquid market in the world because it is a compensation for risk-bearing, not a free lunch."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"PRE: after the close of day t, the first nominal 5y-30y coupon auction of a cluster is exactly h+1 = 4 sessions ahead (next_coupon5_sessions == 4) and no such auction took place in the last two sessions (last_coupon5_sessions >= 3 or absent): TLT and IEF are marked with side -1. POST: day t is an auction day (last_coupon5_sessions == 0) and no further such auction is announced within the next two sessions (next_coupon5_sessions >= 3 or absent): TLT and IEF are marked with side +1. SHY, SHV, BIL, VGSH and SCHO are never marked and are the peers. Both phases are marked, so generic duration drift largely cancels in the placebo mean.","horizons":[1,2,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":3},"notes":"BRIEF FIT. The brief asked for a cross-asset idea (signal from one market, trade in another) with a 1-5 day hold. The lab has exhausted short-horizon cross-asset lead-lag between liquid markets: the 706k-test mrel scan, H-0047, H-0056, H-0070, H-0075, H-0081, H-0087, H-0116 and H-0119 all found nothing, and the only cross-asset passes (H-0114, H-0126) are slow balance-sheet diffusions into single stocks whose books failed. I therefore chose the closest fit with a documented flow and a named counterparty: the signal comes from the Treasury's primary market (the auction calendar from Treasury Fiscal Data, a government macro series like the FRED ones the brief allows) and the trade is in exchange-traded bond funds, a different market whose prices are set by APs and ETF investors. The hold is 3 sessions.
RELATION TO H-0038 (same family, counted as its second trial). H-0038 tested a very similar cycle (short TLT 3 sessions before, long 3 after, SHY as control) and ended with ZERO events at G1 although G0 counted 241, so its mechanism was never measured. K-0086 (written after H-0038) found the most likely cause: G1 needs at least three unmarked peers per date, and H-0038's universe held only TLT and SHY. This card is built around that: five short-Treasury ETFs that are never marked (three from mid-2007), a data period starting after the third peer lists, both phases marked so generic duration drift cancels, explicit cluster rules from the two calendar keys, and the auction session itself excluded from both windows. It is not a parameter rescue of H-0038 (no result exists to tune on). If the Chair considers it a re-run of H-0038, the trial count is the Chair's call; I am filing it under the same family on purpose. If G0 again reports events but G1 none, the cause is not the peer rule and the card should be parked, not resubmitted.
FORECASTS (write-down before data, K-0098/K-0120). Clusters: about two per month (10y/30y mid-month, 5y/7y month-end; 20y from 2020) = about 24 a year x 13.5 years = about 320 clusters. PRE events at lead 4 need the next auction to be announced 4 sessions ahead; most are (announcements come about a week ahead), I expect 80-100 % of clusters. Events: about 2 instruments x (280-320 PRE + 300-320 POST) = 1100-1300 events on 560-640 dates; G1 may count somewhat fewer than G0 (K-0095). Round trip: TLT and IEF are among the most liquid ETFs, I expect about 2-6 bps per round trip in the us_etf tier. Gross per event (3-session abnormal return, averaged over TLT and IEF): pessimistic 3 bps (concession arbitraged away under QE), central 10 bps, optimistic 25 bps (about 1-2 bps of yield on the duration of TLT/IEF). Placebo bar: per-date noise of the TLT/IEF average over 3 sessions is about 1.1 %, so with about 600 dates the 95th percentile sits roughly 7 bps above the placebo mean: the central case passes narrowly, the pessimistic case fails, i.e. this is a fair test, not a 'cannot tell' by design. Mean exposure: windows of 3 + 3 sessions per cluster, about 140 sessions a year out of 252, gross 1.0 inside windows = about 0.5. Book Sharpe: at the central case, per-window Sharpe about 0.1 over about 48 windows a year gives a gross Sharpe near 0.7 and a net Sharpe near 0.5-0.6, so the absolute Sharpe floor vs T-bills (0.5) is the most likely strategy death even if the mechanism passes; the 2007-2020 window also contains three QE programmes in which Fed purchases offset auction supply, which should weaken the middle third.
DESIGN CHOICES. Study and book use the same two instruments and the same windows, so a mechanism pass should translate into the book (avoids the study/book mismatch of K-0064 and H-0044). Equal 0.5 weights are fixed, not tuned. hold_sessions = 3 follows the paper's 'few days before, shortly after'; the lead is tied to it (h+1) so the PRE window always ends at the open of the auction day. Shorts in TLT/IEF carry no modelled borrow cost; both are easy to borrow, but a real implementation would pay a small fee. No forward source exists for ETFs, so G4 is the ceiling (K-0014).","references":[{"cite":"Lou, Yan, Zhang (2013) Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets, Review of Financial Studies 26(8)","year":2013}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: the signal-only calendar dataset treasury_auctions_1d (clock us_close) with keys next_coupon5_sessions (XNYS sessions from day t to the next announced nominal coupon auction with original term >= 5 years, absent if none is announced yet) and last_coupon5_sessions (sessions since the most recent such auction, 0 on the auction day); daily ETF returns (ret_co, ret_oc) of TLT and IEF from sharadar_sfp. Parameter h = hold_sessions (primary 3). Decision after the close of day t, using only values known at that close: (1) PRE event: next_coupon5_sessions[t] == h + 1 AND (last_coupon5_sessions[t] is absent OR last_coupon5_sessions[t] >= 3). That is, the first auction of a cluster is h+1 sessions ahead and no auction happened in the last two sessions. Then hold the PRE book from the open of t+1 to the open of t+h+1 (h sessions, ending at the open of the auction day; the auction session itself is not held). (2) POST event: last_coupon5_sessions[t] == 0 (an auction happened on day t) AND (next_coupon5_sessions[t] is absent OR next_coupon5_sessions[t] >= 3). That is, day t is the last auction of its cluster (auctions on consecutive or next-but-one sessions, e.g. 10y then 30y or 5y then 7y, belong to one cluster). Then hold the POST book from the open of t+1 to the open of t+h+1. Books: PRE = TLT -0.5, IEF -0.5. POST = TLT +0.5, IEF +0.5. If windows overlap on a day, add the weights of all active windows per instrument and clip each instrument to [-0.5, +0.5] (a PRE and a POST window on the same day cancel to flat). Outside windows the book is flat (cash). SHY, SHV, BIL, VGSH and SCHO are never traded; they are in the universe only as unmarked peers for the mechanism test. Gross exposure never exceeds 1.0. Missing data: a window is opened only if the instrument has a price on t and is tradable at t+1; if the calendar keys are absent on t no event fires (no filling, no inferred dates). Index calendar values directly so that a missing series raises instead of silently producing no events (K-0010). Rebalancing is event-driven, with at most one weight change per day.","params":{"hold_sessions":{"grid":[2,3,4],"value":3}},"timeframes":["1d"]},"title":"Treasury auction supply cycle, peer-testable - short TLT/IEF 3 sessions before each 5y-30y auction cluster, long 3 after, short-Treasury ETFs as peers","universe":{"instruments":["TLT","IEF","SHY","SHV","BIL","VGSH","SCHO"],"kind":"instruments"}}

title: Credit-market news into levered equities, plain rule - LIQ-500 beta-tercile-matched long/short on net market leverage in weeks of a credit-specific Baa spread move, hold 5 days

Second likeliest: the plain map fails, which says H-0126's pass needed the coverage/volatility interaction or was luck. Known confounds: financials carry high reported debt and will crowd the HIGH leg (no sector field is loadable; beta terciles partly control it); marketcap is frozen at the filing date (leverage is slow, acceptable); Moody's Baa averages are seasoned bonds and can be stale, which the lagged market term addresses only partly. No references: Merton's structural model is theory, not an anomaly paper, and I did not verify a specific empirical paper for this exact lag.","signal":{"description":"All decisions after the close of the last XNYS session of each calendar week (decision day t), trades at the open of the next session, using only data known by the close of t. (1) Credit shock. Daily spread S_d = DBAA_d - DGS10_d (fred_moody_yields_1d and fred_macro, both clock next_morning, so on day t use values stamped up to t-1 only; days with a missing value carry the last value). Market return M_d = equal-weighted mean of the total daily returns (ret_co + ret_oc compounded) of the LIQ-500 members on day d. Over the 5 sessions ending t-1: dS = change of S, dY = change of DGS10, rM = sum of M, and rM_lag = sum of M over the 5 sessions before those. Regress dS on [1, rM, rM_lag, dY] over non-overlapping 5-session windows of the past 252 sessions ending t-1 (about 50 observations; skip the week if fewer than 40 valid windows). title: Inflation news into nominal balance sheets - LIQ-500 neutral, after a residual TIPS-breakeven shock, real-asset-heavy vs cash-heavy firms within leverage terciles, hold 5 days

Equity investors who think in nominal terms (money illusion, Modigliani and Cohn 1979) and who do not map an inflation-expectations move into each firm's balance-sheet composition reprice the cross-section slowly, so over the following week firms heavy in real assets should beat firms heavy in monetary assets after an up-shock in expected inflation, and the reverse after a down-shock. Both directions of the shock are marked, so the persistent style drift of either leg cancels against the same-stock placebo.","horizons":[1,3,5,10,20],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: the signal comes from the TIPS/Treasury market (FRED breakevens with oil, credit and real-yield controls), the trades are in US stocks, the hold is 5 sessions, and a mechanism test is declared. Family: oil-shock-equity-underreaction is the lab's family for the slow diffusion of macro-price news into stocks through an exposure (H-0056, H-0114, H-0116, H-0119, H-0126, H-0128), so this card counts against it. Banks are excluded by deposits; insurers and brokers stay in (most are in the top leverage tercile). Known confounds I could not remove: monetary-asset-heavy firms are mostly cash-rich tech and healthcare, real-asset-heavy ones are industrials, energy, materials, utilities and REITs, so a sector rotation after reflation news is what is being measured; marking both shock directions and the same-stock placebo net out its average level but not a sector reaction to the news itself, which here is the claim. Expected leg results (K-0172): no prior that one side carries it, since the sides swap with the shock sign; please report the event average by shock sign (inflation up versus down) and by leg. Likeliest death: the mechanism test, with gross under cost or the latest third wrong-signed. If it passes, the part-time dollar-neutral book will most likely miss the absolute Sharpe floor (K-0027); a long-only tilt would then be the next card. No data purchase needed; all series are in the catalog with loaders.","references":[{"cite":"French, Ruback, Schwert (1983) Effects of nominal contracting on stock returns, Journal of Political Economy","year":1983},{"cite":"Modigliani, Cohn (1979) Inflation, rational valuation and the market, Financial Analysts Journal","year":1979}],"signal":{"description":"Timing: decisions once a week after the close of the last XNYS session t of each calendar week, trades at the open of t+1, positions held 5 sessions (exit at the open of t+6), so cohorts do not overlap. Fit OLS y = a + b.x on the trailing 252 sessions of these daily-rolling five-session changes ending at s (needs >= 200 valid rows, otherwise no signal), take the residual e at s and z = e / standard deviation of the window's residuals. A shock week is one with |z| >= z_shock; sign(z) is the direction of the inflation news. Missing FRED days are not filled; a five-session change needs both end values. (2) Balance-sheet exposure, from sharadar_sf1 as reported (arq, usable from the day after filing, stale after 400 days as the loader enforces). Eligible: LIQ-500 member and tradable at t, assets > 0, liabilities present, deposits missing or zero (banks excluded). Monetary-asset share MA = (cashneq + receivables + investmentsc) / assets, a missing component counted as 0. Leverage L = liabilities / assets. Split the eligible stocks into terciles of L on date t; inside each tercile take the bottom leg_quantile of MA (real-asset-heavy) and the top leg_quantile of MA (monetary-asset-heavy). (3) Book. title: TradFi risk shifts re-order the crypto risk ladder, learned - Binance spot top-20 long-only 5-day cohorts, LightGBM on beta/ivol/liquidity x VIX and real-yield shifts
card_json: {"asset_classes":["crypto_spot"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"binance_spot_1d","description":"tradable universe, point-in-time top 20 USDT pairs by 30-day quote volume; start after Binance had about twenty USDT pairs","frequency":"1d","period":["2018-07-01","2022-12-31"]},{"dataset":"fred_macro","description":"signal only: VIX close and 10-year TIPS real yield, clock next_morning","fields":["VIXCLS","DFII10"],"frequency":"1d"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: on TradFi shock dates the gbm-only picks (side +1) minus ridge-only picks (side -1) do not beat the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos at 5 days, or the gross abnormal return per event is below the round-trip cost, or fewer than two of three blocks have the predicted sign.","Mechanism kill condition (K-0060): the latest third of dev (which holds the real-yield tightening of the dev window) has the wrong sign, even if the pooled test passes.","Ridge on the same features is as good: the ridge-only picks earn as much as or more than the gbm-only picks on shock dates (event average at or below zero), i.e. the TradFi state does not re-order the ladder.","If the disagreement average on calm dates (descriptive, not gated) is as large as on shock dates, the gain is coin-feature nonlinearity, not the cross-asset channel, and the card's mechanism is refuted even if the event test passes.","Net Sharpe on dev below BTC buy-and-hold Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference at or below zero.","Fewer than 75 % of the neighbors of n_estimators 100 and top 0.2 beat BTC buy-and-hold, or Sharpe at doubled costs below BTC buy-and-hold."],"family":"crypto-flight-to-quality","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Levered and VaR-constrained altcoin holders (margin traders, crypto funds facing redemptions from TradFi allocators) who must sell high-beta, illiquid coins with a lag after a US risk-off shift and accept the price concession over several days; on risk-on shifts, late re-risking buyers who chase high-beta coins after BTC has already moved.","why":"Crypto holdings form a risk ladder: BTC (deepest market, the collateral asset), then ETH and large coins, then high-beta, high-idiosyncratic-risk, thinner altcoins held by levered retail and by crypto funds whose capital comes partly from TradFi allocators. When US risk appetite shifts (US implied equity volatility jumps, or the US real yield jumps, which tightens dollar funding), VaR- and margin-constrained holders cut risk, and they cut it from the top of the ladder: high-beta, illiquid altcoins are sold and capital moves toward BTC or stablecoins (flight to quality and to liquidity, Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009). Margin limits are updated on trailing volatility and fund redemptions are processed with a lag, so the rotation is spread over several days after the shift and the TradFi signal is still informative one to two days late. After a risk-on shift (VIX or real yield falling) the reverse rotation runs: re-risking capital enters through BTC and moves up the ladder over the following days. The claim is therefore conditional: which coins win over the next five days depends on the interaction of a date-level TradFi shift with the coin's place on the ladder, and the sign of the ladder premium flips between risk-off and risk-on shifts.","why_not_arbitraged":"Front-running the rotation requires shorting altcoins (borrow is scarce on spot, perp funding and squeeze risk are high) or holding concentrated altcoin longs into stress; the arbitrage capital that could do it is itself funding-constrained in exactly these states (funding-liquidity spiral). Daily crypto lead-lag to US macro series is not the claim: the information is a slow-moving constraint on holders, not news to be priced."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"On a decision date where the TradFi state shifted (|dvix5| >= 0.15, a 5-observation log change of VIX of at least 15 %, or |dry5| >= 0.15 percentage points, a 5-observation change of the 10-year real yield), a coin is in the top `top` fraction (0.2 = top fifth) of the gbm score but not in the same top fraction of the ridge score on the same features (side +1), or in the ridge's top fraction but not the gbm's (side -1).","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"ml":{"features":["beta60: 60-day OLS beta of the coin's daily total return on BTCUSDT, z-scored across members (place on the crypto risk ladder: how much the coin is sold per unit of crypto-wide de-risking)","ivol60: 60-day residual volatility from the same regression, z-scored (idiosyncratic risk that margin and VaR systems penalize and that a BTC hedge cannot remove)","liq30: log 30-day median daily quote volume, z-scored (liquidity ladder: flight to liquidity hits thin coins hardest)","dvix5: 5-observation log change of VIX (FRED VIXCLS, next_morning clock), date-level, raw (US equity risk-appetite shift)","dry5: 5-observation change of the 10-year TIPS real yield (FRED DFII10, next_morning clock), date-level, raw (dollar funding / discount-rate tightening shift)","lvix: log VIX level, date-level, raw (whether the shift happens in a calm or an already stressed state, where VaR limits bind harder)"],"horizon_days":5,"model":"gbm","retrain_every_days":63,"why_not_linear":"The label is ranked across coins on each date, so a date-level input (dvix5, dry5, lvix) adds the same constant to every coin's linear score and cannot change the ranking: a ridge on these six features can only learn the unconditional ladder premium from beta60, ivol60 and liq30 and is blind to the TradFi state by construction. The mechanism says the ladder premium changes sign with the direction of the TradFi shift (risk-off: low beta, low ivol, liquid coins win; risk-on: the reverse) and is larger when VIX is already high, which is a state x characteristic interaction that a tree expresses with a split on dvix5 or dry5 followed by a split on beta60 or liq30. The ridge on the same features is therefore the exact control for 'the TradFi state adds nothing'. Who pays: the margin- and VaR-constrained altcoin holders who de-risk with a lag (risk-off) and the late chasers of high-beta coins (risk-on)."},"notes":"Why this fits the brief: signals from the US equity-options and Treasury markets (FRED VIX and real yield), trades in crypto spot; 5-day horizon; a walk-forward gbm whose only possible gain over a ridge on the same features is the state x characteristic interaction (ranked labels make date-level inputs invisible to a linear score). Difference from earlier cards: H-0081 sorted on the day's BTC-residual return under a VIX-level gate and bet on reversal (liquidity provision); this card has no return feature at all, sorts on the ex-ante ladder position (beta, idiosyncratic risk, liquidity) and claims that the sign of the ladder premium follows the direction of the TradFi shift; it is neither the H-0081 sort nor its mirror. H-0124 switched coin momentum by VIX and BTC-trend states and never produced a score (K-0170); this card shares the VIX input, so the Chair may merge families if it reads them as one mechanism (state-switched crypto sort), and I would accept that. Scoring safeguards against the H-0124 failure modes (inferred, not verified): no feature needs more than 60 days, the date-level features must not be passed through the cross-sectional z-score helper (that would make them zero or NaN on every row and could leave no complete rows), spot data from mid-2018 gives about 4.5 years of dev so the first refit has data, and the walk-forward runs on all columns with non-members masked per row (K-0134). A zero-event G0 should be read as a bug, not a mechanism result. Universe start: from memory Binance listed few USDT pairs before 2018, so the period starts mid-2018; if lab check or G0 shows fewer than about 15 members early on, the fewer-than-10 rule keeps those cohorts in cash. Forecasts (K-0120, K-0165): scored dates about 1200-1300 after the model's first fit; shock dates (|dvix5| >= 0.15 or |dry5| >= 0.15 pp, weekends included because the feature is carried) about 35-40 % of them, i.e. 400-500 dates; disagreement events are model-defined, range 300-2500 (1-3 coins per side per shock date). If the gbm almost never disagrees with the ridge the event count fails: that reads as 'no state dependence found', the same verdict as a failed placebo. Round trip for top-20 spot pairs about 30-60 bps (10 bps fee per side plus slippage); gross per event central about 60 bps, pessimistic 0, optimistic 150 at 5 days, so the cost check is likely to bind (K-0053). Blocks: the first third (mid-2018 to early 2020) is partly empty from model warm-up (K-0163), so both later thirds must be positive. Beta confound (K-0074): on risk-off dates the gbm-only picks are probably lower beta than the ridge-only picks, so if crypto keeps falling after US risk-off shifts the test is positive partly through market direction; that continuation is part of the claimed de-risking, but a pure crypto time-series drift after US shocks would look the same and is not separated here. Please report the event average separately for risk-off shifts (dvix5 or dry5 up) and risk-on shifts, and for calm dates. Book arithmetic: always invested, exposure about 1.0, daily cohorts of 4 coins at 5 % each; on calm days the score is persistent, so expected turnover is roughly 20-40x a year and cost drag 6-15 % a year at 30-60 bps round trip, i.e. about 0.1-0.2 Sharpe at crypto volatility. The book must beat BTC buy-and-hold by 0.10 Sharpe with a long-only altcoin-heavy book over a window with two altcoin bear phases; that is the likeliest death after the mechanism test. title: Home-holiday delayed anchoring - fade an Asian country ETF's US-hours move while its home exchange stays closed, peer-hedged, hold to reopening

They demand immediacy in the direction of the US move. Market makers and authorized participants take the other side, but the basket cannot be traded and creation and redemption against a stale NAV is risky or suspended on home holidays. So they quote wider and lean prices with inventory. The liquidity demander pays the overshoot, which comes back at the reopening.","why":"A US-listed Asia-Pacific country ETF trades during US hours while its home market is shut. Its price then moves on US information and US order flow with no underlying basket to anchor it. Levy and Lieberman (2013) document that country ETFs overreact to US market returns in these non-synchronous hours, and that the overreaction corrects when the home market next trades. On a normal day that correction happens in the Asian session, overnight before the next US open. A taker who trades at the open cannot reach it: it shows up in the close-to-open return. A scheduled home-market holiday pushes the next home session past the next US open. A US-hours move made on the eve of the holiday then stays unanchored through one more full US session, and its correction comes only when the home market reopens. That window can be traded open to open. The signal comes from one market (the home exchange's calendar and the absence of its price discovery) and the trade happens in another (the US-listed wrapper). It is hedged with Asian peer ETFs whose home markets did reopen, whose US prices already contain the correction.","why_not_arbitraged":"The arbitrage link is physically cut: no underlying trades and the NAV is stale, so an AP cannot lock in the gap. Hedging with index futures is only partial: some home futures are closed too, and others trade in thin off-hours sessions. A holiday-eve position carries one or more days of gap risk across the reopening, in single small markets with modest capacity, on irregular dates that differ by country. That is unattractive for large arbitrage desks and invisible to anyone who trades only the normal overnight correction."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the US close of day t, a listed Asia-Pacific country ETF whose home exchange has no session before the next US open (closed_next = 1) has an unanchored US-hours move U (since its last home-anchored open) with |U| >= min_z times its vol_days open-to-close volatility. Side = -sign(U): the ETF should underperform the other instruments after an up move and outperform after a down move once its home market reopens. Unmarked peers are the other listed ETFs on the same date, including the Asian ETFs whose home markets reopen before the next US open, EFA and SPY.","horizons":[1,2,3,5],"primary_horizon_days":2},"notes":"Brief fit: short horizon (1-3 sessions, mostly one), cross-asset in the sense of the brief. The signal is the state of another market (the home exchange is closed, so no price discovery there) together with the ETF's US-hours move, which mostly comes from the US market. The trade is in the US-listed wrapper, hedged with wrappers whose home markets did reopen. FRED is not needed. Family: filed under etf-premium-arbitrage because the mechanism is a wrapper deviating from an underlying that cannot be arbitraged against. The trials of H-0037, H-0043, H-0077-H-0080 and H-0090 count against it. Why this is not a retry of the dead ETF-gap cards: K-0105 and H-0037/H-0080 traded daily closes of ETFs while the underlying basket was open, so any wrapper gap closed inside the day and before the next open. Here the event is defined by the underlying being shut through the next US open. On normal days (which the time-shifted placebos mostly sample) the correction falls in the close-to-open return the strategy cannot earn. On holiday eves it is delayed into the open-to-open window. So the placebo comparison is the natural control: the same kind of move on days when the home market reopens overnight should show nothing from the next open on.
